articles.title: Gina Rinehart bankrolls purchase of 10% stake in Seven network owner Southern Cross Media | Gina Rinehart | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Gina Rinehart, Australia’s richest person, has provided a loan to Bruce McWilliam for his acquisition of a nearly 10% stake in Southern Cross Media, which owns the Seven Network and other media brands. The investment, worth approximately $26 million, gives Rinehart significant influence over the company's future despite not directly owning shares.  This move marks Rinehart’s return to the media industry after a previous foray into the sector with Ten Network and Fairfax Media.

articles.title: HDFC Bank shares fall 2% on reports of internal probe over Rs 45 cr interest payments - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: HDFC Bank allegedly routed differential interest payments to the Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC), a state government agency, through its marketing department disguised as road safety awareness campaign sponsorship. This practice violated RBI regulations and the bank's own anti-bribery policy. The bank’s former chairman, Atanu Chakraborty, resigned on March 18th citing ethical concerns related to these practices.  The bank's share prices have declined significantly since the resignation.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Alleged abuse of power and violation of regulations by a major bank raises serious concerns.

articles.title: Adani Power surpasses Infosys in market capitalisation after 126% rally in one year - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Adani Power's stock surged to become India's 11th most valued company, driven by soaring power demand fueled by the intense El Niño year and heatwave conditions.  The surge comes as India grapples with record-breaking temperatures, placing it among the world's hottest cities. Infosys, meanwhile, saw its share price decline due to concerns about the impact of AI advancements on the software-as-a-service market.

articles.title: Taiwan’s economy is booming thanks to AI. Not everyone sees the benefits | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Taiwan's economy is experiencing rapid growth due to its semiconductor industry, which powers leading AI models.  However, this boom has raised concerns about wealth inequality and the uneven distribution of benefits. While the stock market has seen significant gains, many Taiwanese workers in non-tech sectors are facing rising costs for housing and living expenses. The Central Bank Governor Yang Chin-lung has sounded the alarm about an "K-shaped economy," where certain sectors grow rapidly while others stagnate.  Some argue that Taiwan's economic model is becoming too reliant on a single industry, leaving other sectors behind.

articles.title: Supreme Court sets aside NCLAT order which rejected Amazon's appeal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court overturned the decisions of the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) and the Competition Commission of India (CCI) regarding Amazon's investment deal with Future Group. The court ruled that the NCLAT and CCI orders, which had rejected Amazon's appeal and levied a penalty on it, were invalid.  The Supreme Court ordered the refund of any amounts deposited or recovered from Amazon based on these orders within eight weeks.

articles.title: LIC shares drop 4% on Rs 10,000 crore govt stake sale buzz - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The government plans to sell a 2% stake in the state-run insurer, Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), to institutional investors in late June or early July.  The Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) is working with financial institutions including Goldman Sachs Group, Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors, BNP Paribas SA, and IIFL Capital Services to manage the transaction. LIC has been given until May 2032 to meet regulatory requirements for a minimum public shareholding of 25%.  The insurer recently announced its first-ever bonus issue in a ratio of 1:1.

articles.title: Top gold loan companies expand bullion holdings to record levels in FY26 - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: India's gold imports fell by nearly 5% year-on-year to 721 tonnes in FY26, according to commerce ministry data.  IIFL Finance saw its gold holdings rise due to regulatory action lifting restrictions on the company's gold loan business. Muthoot Finance saw a decline in gold holdings, while Manappuram Finance reported a record high in gold holdings.

articles.title: Listed brokers, exchanges rake in profits even as war clouds linger - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: BSE and NSE reported strong financial performance in the March quarter, with consolidated profit after tax increasing by 33% and 19%, respectively.  Standalone revenues for listed brokers like Groww, Angel One, and Anand Rathi Share & Stock Brokers rose between 3% and 23%, while standalone profits increased by 11%.  Kotak Securities attributed the performance to a favorable base effect, higher market volatility, and diversification beyond core broking income.   Brokers are evolving into "pseudo-NBFCs" with products like algo trading gaining traction.

articles.title: Islamabad plans oil reserves, storage push - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's energy ministry is proposing to build strategic petroleum reserves and commercial storage through bonded terminals, refineries, and oil marketing companies to increase its energy security. The government plans to cut reliance on imports from the Strait of Hormuz by boosting domestic production and refining capacity.  The proposed framework, shared with international oil producers and trading firms, aims to create commercial inventories that could support domestic supply during emergencies.

articles.title: Sensex falls 70 points, Nifty below 23,900 as US-Iran tensions simmer - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Sensex opened lower on Wednesday, declining around 70 points to reach near 75,940. The Nifty 50 also fell over 33 points, opening at 23,880.  Despite this, the India VIX dropped more than 3%. While some stocks like Sun Pharma and ITC saw gains, others such as HDFC Bank, Infosys, and Axis Bank experienced losses. Analysts suggest that the Indian market is being weighed down by foreign institutional investor (FII) selling due to global markets' bull rally.  However, analysts also highlight positive developments from Q4 results, including strong midcap performance and profit growth outpacing revenue growth.

articles.title: Paul Keating urges Labor to stick with capital gains tax overhaul and avoid exemptions that would hurt economy | Tax | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Paul Keating urged Labor to maintain its stance on controversial capital gains tax changes, warning that exempting commercial assets would further distort the economy.  The architect of major economic reforms in the 1980s and 90s, Keating argued that correcting the balance between capital and labor taxation should be a priority. The treasurer, Jim Chalmers, has also expressed concerns about creating new distortions in the tax system. However, investors and entrepreneurs are fiercely opposed to the government's plans, warning they will hinder investment and risk-taking.  The legislation is expected to include changes to negative gearing rules, a $1,000 standard tax deduction, and a new $250-a-year tax offset for workers.

articles.title: Senco Gold shares fall 3% despite 151% jump in Q4 net profit; firm tops FY26 guidance - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Senco Gold reported a 45% increase in revenue from operations to Rs 1,996.7 crore for the fourth quarter of FY26, driven by higher gold, silver, and platinum prices. The company's EBITDA margin also improved significantly, reaching 13.7%.  The retail sales reached an all-time high of Rs 1,731 crore with a 35% year-on-year growth. Senco Gold expanded its showroom network to 201 outlets during the fiscal year and achieved a 33% year-on-year revenue growth exceeding its stated FY26 guidance.

articles.title: Top 10 countries with fastest billionaire growth by 2031: Saudi Arabia, Poland and Sweden top the global wealth race | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: World of Statistics (formerly Twitter) predicts a significant rise in billionaire populations globally over the next few years, with notable shifts occurring outside traditional Western economic centers. Saudi Arabia, driven by diversification away from oil dependence, stands out for its rapid growth, while Poland experiences acceleration fueled by manufacturing strength and technology outsourcing. Sweden, Australia, Denmark, Japan, Mexico, and the Philippines also show varying degrees of growth, with factors like technology, green industries, and services-based expansion playing key roles.  These trends suggest a more fragmented and dynamic wealth landscape than previously anticipated.

articles.title: Many airlines are not launching new routes due to surge in oil prices: BIAL MD and CEO - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kempegowda International Airport (KIA) is facing increased pressure from rising oil prices, impacting airline profitability and prompting route cancellations. Hari Marar, managing director of BIAL, stated that the crisis will continue to affect airlines until oil prices stabilize.  Despite this, some airlines have seen an increase in frequency on existing routes, while new routes are being launched by European carriers like SWISS and Qantas.

articles.title: Fuel shortage hits pumps amid panic buying; OMCs call for calm, say supply is steady - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Farmers across several states in India are facing fuel shortages due to the recent hike in fuel prices.  The Centre has implemented price hikes to mitigate losses for its oil marketing companies (OMCs), but this has led to supply disruptions and long queues at petrol stations.  In Maharashtra, farmers are struggling to procure diesel for their tractors, while in Punjab, the Punjab Petrol Pump Dealers Association reports short supplies of both petrol and diesel. The situation is impacting agricultural activities and transportation, with some fuel stations even running dry.  The Petroleum Ministry has assured the public that there is no shortage of fuel but urged people to avoid panic buying.

articles.title: NA panel takes govt to task over budget preparation, reforms - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A parliamentary committee in Pakistan expressed concern over the government's failure to circulate and publish the Budget Strategy Paper by May 10th, as well as its continued reliance on indirect taxes and petroleum levy. Syed Naveed Qamar, former finance minister of the PPP, criticized the lack of progress on structural reforms and highlighted the growing burden of circular debt in the energy sector.  Dr Ali Salman, a private economist representing the UNDP, warned that inflation could undermine economic growth due to rising prices for essential goods. The committee also expressed concern about Pakistan's dependence on foreign imports and the vulnerability of the economy to regional geopolitical instability.

articles.title: White House proposes NDAs for all US federal workers | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The White House has proposed a guideline requiring all US federal workers to sign non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) to prevent unauthorized disclosure of sensitive information. The proposal, announced by the Office of Personnel Management, would allow the White House to take legal action against employees who violate the agreement and asserts that the government is entitled to royalties from disclosing such information.  The White House has faced criticism for its aggressive campaign against news outlets and media figures critical of it, including threats to revoke licenses of ABC stations and restricting reporters' access at the Pentagon.

articles.title: US stocks today: S&P 500 hits record closing high on AI optimism, Micron joins $1 trillion club - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: U.S. equities rallied on Tuesday, driven by upbeat earnings and renewed confidence in the AI trade, despite ongoing tensions with Iran.  Chris Zaccarelli, chief investment officer for Northlight Asset Management, likened the current market rally to the tech boom of the late 1990s.  U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressed optimism that a deal with Iran could be reached soon, while Adam Sarhan, CEO of 50 Park Investments, noted the likelihood of a peaceful resolution. The S&P 500, Nasdaq Composite, and Russell 2000 touched record highs, fueled by strong earnings growth and positive sentiment towards AI.

articles.title: India’s energy strategy needs price correction - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Strait of Hormuz crisis has exposed the interconnectedness of energy security and geopolitics, impacting global crude markets and transportation costs. India, heavily reliant on imported oil, has implemented a combination of state intervention, supply diversification, and financial absorption to mitigate the impact on consumers. While petrol and diesel prices have remained relatively stable in India compared to other advanced economies, the country's reliance on fossil fuels remains a structural vulnerability. The government is facing pressure to implement a more sustainable approach to fuel pricing, balancing economic realities with consumer needs.

articles.title: ​U-Turn! MFs pull back from 12 smallcap stocks after two quarters of buying - Turning Tide | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Mutual fund (MF) shareholdings in BSE smallcap stocks have reversed course, with a notable decrease in holdings across several companies.  Newgen Software Technologies, Ecos (India) Mobility & Hospitality, Bajaj Electricals, and Updater Services saw significant reductions in their MF holdings during the March 2026 quarter compared to previous quarters. This trend suggests a shift away from long-term investment strategies, with some companies experiencing substantial declines in value over the past year.

articles.title: Labor to announce easing of jobseeker mutual obligations requirements in major overhaul of employment system | Unemployment | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Amanda Rishworth, the Australian Minister for Social Services, will outline plans to overhaul the country's employment system.  She is expected to criticize the current mutual obligation regime as "ill-equipped" and ineffective in helping unemployed Australians find work.  Rishworth will propose a new model with three streams of support tailored to individual needs, aiming to address concerns about unfairness and inadequate job placement assistance. The government plans to engage in consultation on the proposed changes before finalizing them.

articles.title: Sebi chief Tuhin Kanta Pandey backs bond ETFs, tokenisation as debt fundraising nears Rs 9 lakh crore - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey highlighted the growing importance of India's debt market, noting that it has raised nearly Rs 9 lakh crore in FY26, almost double the amount raised by the equity market.  He emphasized the need for deeper development of the corporate bond market to support long-term economic growth and urged greater retail participation and reduced dependence on bank-led financing. Sebi is exploring initiatives such as bond ETFs, stronger disclosures, tokenization pilots, and outreach programs to improve investor awareness and accessibility in fixed-income products.  Pandey stressed that regulation must evolve with market structures and emerging risks.

articles.title: Fredun Pharmaceuticals board approves 2:1 bonus issue - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Fredun's Board of Directors recommended a 2:1 bonus share issuance to reward shareholders for their long-term commitment and confidence in the company's growth. The move is driven by strong financial performance, including total revenues of Rs 639.12 crore and an EBITDA of Rs 94.79 Cr in FY26. This decision reflects Fredun's confidence in its ability to sustain this growth trajectory across various high-growth segments like branded generic exports, domestic formulations, pet healthcare, nutraceuticals, and cosmeceuticals.

articles.title: Renters could save $20bn on bills in a decade from rooftop solar and appliance upgrades – if landlords act | Energy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Landlords are not motivated to upgrade rental properties with energy efficiency measures like insulation, appliances, and solar panels due to the lack of financial incentive. The Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis (IEEFA) found that a combination of upgrades could save renters $20 billion within a decade, while also easing strain on power networks.  The IEEFA recommends regulation requiring landlords to meet minimum energy efficiency standards and offering incentives like tax breaks for upgraded properties.

articles.title: 'India more diversified:' Sebi chief Tuhin Kanta Pandey comments on Taiwan's market ascent - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Taiwan’s market cap surpassed India’s to become the world's fifth-largest equity market, driven largely by TSMC.  This surge is fueled by investor interest in semiconductor and AI-linked companies. While India faces challenges from high oil prices, foreign outflows, and slower earnings growth, its broader economic fundamentals remain larger than Taiwan’s. Despite this, the diversification of India's market capitalisation provides greater resilience during sector-specific volatility.

articles.title: HFCL shares rally 22% in just 5 sessions. Here’s what technical charts indicate - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: HFCL stock has experienced a strong bullish breakout and sustained buying momentum, with prices rallying on good volumes.  Analysts believe the stock is currently in an uptrend, supported by institutional activity and positive financial results. Ruchit Jain, Vice President of Technical Research at Motilal Oswal, suggests traders with existing longs should hold onto their positions while Harshal Dasani, Business Head at INVasset PMS, notes that the breakout may be a short-term phenomenon.  Kunal Kamble, Sr. Technical Research Analyst at Bonanza, agrees, highlighting aggressive accumulation and confidence among market participants.

articles.title: Jefferies raises target price of auto ancillary stock that's venturing into aerospace - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Jefferies, an investment bank, has upgraded its rating on Belrise Industries to "Buy" with a revised price target of Rs 250. The upgrade is based on the company's strong March quarter performance and positive medium-term earnings outlook.  The brokerage anticipates Belrise's revenue growth to be driven by new orders in the two-wheeler, four-wheeler, aerospace, and defense sectors. Jefferies expects Belrise's EBITDA and EPS to grow at a 26% CAGR over FY26–28. Despite potential risks including high dependence on its top customer, Belrise Industries, the brokerage maintains its "Buy" rating with a target price of Rs 250 based on a 26 times multiple on March FY28 earnings per share.

articles.title: First Taiwan, then South Korea? How global AI supercycle is demoting Indian stock market - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Taiwan’s market capitalization reached $4.95 trillion, surpassing India’s value of $4.92 trillion, driven by the surge in Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC).  This rise is attributed to TSMC's dominance in the AI supply chain and regulatory changes favoring its shares. Meanwhile, India faces challenges due to a lack of exposure to the AI and semiconductor cycle, leading to foreign portfolio investor outflows and weak relative earnings growth. This decline has resulted in a decrease in India’s weight in the MSCI emerging markets index.

articles.title: Sri Lanka jolts markets with outsized 100-bp rate hike to counter Gulf crisis - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sri Lanka's Central Bank raised its overnight policy rate by 100 basis points to 8.75% in response to higher inflation and a depreciating rupee due to the ongoing U.S.-Israeli war with Iran. This move, the biggest since March 2023, signals a shift from supporting growth to prioritizing price stability. Economists predict slowing economic growth to 3.0% in 2026, down from the initial projection of 4.2%.  The central bank expects the impact of the Iran conflict on inflation to be prolonged and sticky.

articles.title: Suzlon Energy shares rise after Q4 results. What are Motilal Oswal, Nuvama saying? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Suzlon Energy's revenue surged 45% year-on-year to Rs 5,468 crore during the March quarter.  The company's net profit jumped 150% from the previous quarter and EBITDA increased by 39%. However, its EBITDA margin dipped to 17.6%, down from 18.4% in the same period last year. Nuvama Institutional Equities downgraded the stock to 'Hold', citing competition from solar and battery energy storage projects.  Meanwhile, Motilal Oswal maintained a "Buy" rating with a target price of Rs 65, highlighting the company's strong position in commercial and industrial segments but also noting potential pressure on working capital due to the growing EPC business.

articles.title: CNG prices hiked fourth time in eleven days in Delhi and North India; latest by ₹2/kg - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Indraprastha Gas Ltd (IGL) increased the price of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) in Delhi by ₹2 per kilogram on Tuesday, marking the fourth hike in eleven days. This follows a pattern seen across other city-gas distributors who have implemented price increases in smaller increments due to rising input gas costs and geopolitical tensions. Mahanagar Gas Ltd (MGL) in Mumbai also discontinued subsidies for commercial customers citing similar reasons.

articles.title: Power bills to fall by up to 10% from July as renewables and batteries soar across Australia | Energy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Australian Energy Regulator (AER) chair Clare Savage announced that energy bills for households and small businesses will fall by up to 10% in eastern states due to increased renewable energy sources like solar and batteries. The AER final offer for 2026-27 predicts a 3.4% to 10.7% decrease for households on standing offers, with savings of up to $155 per year. Small businesses across three states will also see price reductions, ranging from 5% to 20.9%. The Clean Energy Council warned that investment in new wind and solar projects is declining, potentially hindering the energy transition's progress.

articles.title: Silver dips Rs 3,800/kg, gold at Rs 1.58 lakh/10 gms after US attacks southern Iran in fresh strikes. Should you sell? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: MCX silver futures fell 1.3% to Rs 2,72,985 per kg on July 2026 delivery, while gold futures for June 2026 delivery declined 0.7% to Rs 1,58,534 per 10 grams.  U.S. Central Command conducted strikes in southern Iran targeting boats and missile launch sites, aiming to protect U.S. troops from Iranian threats. Oil prices rose over 2%, influenced by inflation expectations, while spot gold slipped 0.7% to $4,537.54 per ounce.

articles.title: Premier Energies shares gain 4% after Nomura, Quant, others purchase stake in Rs 2,289 crore bulk deal - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Smallcap World Fund Inc, Quant Mutual Fund, and Nomura India Investment Fund Mother Fund purchased significant shares in solar equipment maker Premier Energies, following a large promoter family share sale worth Rs 2,289 crore. The transaction saw several institutional investors participating in the company's growth, driven by investor interest in renewable energy and domestic manufacturing.  Premier Energies reported strong Q4 FY26 earnings with revenue growth of 38% year-on-year and a profit after tax increase of 64%. The company is expanding its module and cell manufacturing capacities, as well as venturing into transformers and power equipment through Transcom.

articles.title: Cost of living crisis reshapes Eid spending in Nigeria | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Families in Nigeria are adjusting their Eid al-Adha celebrations due to rising costs. Yunus Akanji, an Islamic teacher, is canceling his annual trip to Saki and hosting a modest celebration at his madrassa in Abuja because of financial strain. Nafisa Ibrahim, a graduate volunteer, has abandoned plans to travel home for the holiday due to high transport costs.  Opeyemi Ibrahim, a fashion designer, reports decreased customer patronage as fuel prices and electricity supply disruptions impact his business. At livestock markets, sellers are struggling with rising prices of animals and transportation. The overall effect is that many families are cutting back on celebrations and basic necessities.

articles.title: Pine Labs shares rise over 4% after Q4 results. Why Morgan Stanley forecasts 67% upside - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Pine Labs' revenue for Q4FY26 rose 17% year-on-year to Rs 701 crore, exceeding expectations. The company reported a profit after tax of Rs 113 crore for the fiscal year, reversing a loss from the previous year. Morgan Stanley maintained its "Equal-weight" rating on Pine Labs, citing strong growth in issuing and acquiring businesses and improved operating leverage. Despite geopolitical tensions impacting international operations, Pine Labs ended FY26 with net cash of Rs 24.5 billion.

articles.title: HC dismisses bank’s plea against DRAT order - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana High Court declined to intervene in an order from the Debt Recovery Appellate Tribunal-Kolkata, which dismissed a petition by Bank of Baroda (e-Vijaya bank) seeking to condone delay in appealing a debt recovery tribunal order. The court upheld the decision to dismiss the writ petition, affirming the DRT-Hyderabad's 2019 ruling requiring the bank to refund ₹4.64 crore with simple interest to Kosetty Krishna.

articles.title: FM Sitharaman says Government open to hear investor concerns on LTCG, STCG taxation - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman stated that the government is open to receiving feedback and suggestions from investors regarding capital gains taxation.  She emphasized the government's willingness to listen to stakeholders on this issue, particularly amidst growing concerns over market participation and investor sentiment due to global geopolitical tensions and economic uncertainties. Sitharaman also clarified that recent petrol and diesel price hikes are driven by global procurement realities rather than policy changes, highlighting the government's commitment to protecting consumers from shocks.

articles.title: CD rates on the rise could soon bring more on retail deposits - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Bankers and analysts are predicting that deposit rates will increase as one-year CD rates rise to 7.70%, driven by tighter liquidity in the banking system. This is due to a shrinking gap between government treasury bill yields and CD rates, with average daily banking system liquidity now at ₹50,000 crore compared to ₹3 lakh crore in April.  The expectation is that retail deposit rates will follow suit as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)'s policy rate moves, though the exact timing and magnitude remain uncertain.

articles.title: A.P. Ministers review excise reforms, liquor policy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh's high-level ministerial sub-committee on excise policies met to review reforms, revenue enhancement measures, and long-term policy decisions. The meeting, attended by officials from the Excise and Mines Department, Health Department, and Energy Department, discussed proposals for continuing the current liquor policy, restructuring licence fee slabs, and rationalizing liquor outlets.  The committee also reviewed proposals to revise beer and liquor prices due to rising input costs and global disruptions, as well as measures to improve beer supply and address seasonal demand fluctuations.

articles.title: Dy. CM asks Singareni to bag new mines in other States - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Deputy Chief Minister M. Bhatti Vikramarka urged Singareni Collieries Company Ltd. to secure new coal blocks in other states and produce high-quality coal to compete in the market.  He criticized the previous BRS government for failing to acquire these mines despite being in power for 10 years, and promised to review progress on suggestions from elected representatives every fortnight. The meeting included ministers, legislators, advisors, and officials from the energy department.

articles.title: Oil PSUs report sharp rise in demand for diesel, petrol in Telangana - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Telangana is experiencing a surge in petroleum product demand due to agricultural activities and increased retail consumer preference for PSU oil marketing companies (IOC, BPCL, HPCL) over private firms.  Sales of diesel and petrol at PSU outlets have seen significant growth, with 12 districts recording sales increases between 15-25% and five districts exceeding 25%. Despite fuel price hikes by OMCs, the supply chain remains stable as IOC, BPCL, and HPCL are coordinating operations to ensure uninterrupted availability of petrol, diesel, and LPG across the state.

articles.title: Tim Hortons says it will hire 10,000 locals in Canada amid boycott call, 'Singh Hortons' nickname - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Tim Hortons, the restaurant chain, announced a shift away from its reliance on Temporary Foreign Worker (TFW) programs and will prioritize hiring 10,000 local workers as it expands across Canada.  The company's parent company, Restaurant Brands, stated that they have not lobbied for TFW program changes and are committed to hiring locally. The spokesperson clarified that the wage structure is consistent for all employees and that there was never a preference for cheap labor.

articles.title: Bolivia’s embattled president says will take a 50 percent salary cut | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Bolivia’s President Rodrigo Paz announced a 50% salary cut for himself and his cabinet ministers, citing the move as a commitment to the country amidst growing political unrest. Protests demanding his resignation have caused supply chain disruptions in major cities, leading to shortages of food, fuel, and medicine. The protests stem from concerns about Paz's alignment with business interests and his lack of representation from Indigenous or working-class groups.

articles.title: Bengaluru: Toyota BizIntel Hub to come up at KWIN City with ₹1,200 cr. investment - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Toyota Kirloskar Motor (TKM) signed an agreement with the Karnataka government to establish its global-standard BizIntel Hub at KWIN City in Bengaluru. The project, valued at ₹1,200 crore, will create approximately 200 jobs and encompass vehicle manufacturing, testing activities, and an advanced automobile manufacturing facility.  The first phase of the project involves 300 acres of land allotted to TKM, with a projected investment of ₹48,000 crore across five phases. The initiative aims to foster innovation, healthcare, and information technology in KWIN City.

articles.title: PSX opens shortened trading week on bullish note; KSE-100 gains 4,000 points during intraday trade - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Stock Exchange’s (PSX) benchmark index surged over 4,000 points on Monday, closing at 171,857.41 points, a gain of 2.39 percent. The market opened with bullish momentum, gaining 3,594 points from Friday's close.  The rally was driven by hopes for an imminent US-Iran deal to open the Strait of Hormuz and eased concerns over potential oil supply disruptions. Oil prices also fell on Monday.

articles.title: Farmers are an integral part of alco-bev industry, do not leave them behind: Timmapur urges industry - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: R.B. Timmapur, Excise Minister of Karnataka, emphasized the importance of farmers in the state's alcohol-beverage industry, stating that they are integral to the supply chains of breweries.  He urged for inclusive growth and highlighted the government's commitment to expanding the sector through policy reforms aimed at simplifying regulations and promoting sustainability initiatives. Shivkumar Eashwaran, chairman of the Indian Chamber of Commerce, also emphasized the importance of sustainable practices in shaping the future of the alco-bev industry.

articles.title: Oil prices fall below $100 a barrel on hopes of Iran peace deal | Oil | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Oil prices fell below $100 a barrel on Monday, with Brent crude futures dropping 6% to $97.28 a barrel as hopes for a US-Iran peace deal fueled optimism in the stock market. While negotiations have progressed, key issues remain unresolved, including Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.  Analysts caution that a return to normal oil flows will take months and that damaged energy infrastructure may persist. Despite this uncertainty, stock markets rose across Europe and Asia as investors reacted positively to potential easing of tensions in the region.

articles.title: Why foreign investors are exiting Nifty giants to hunt in India's small and midcap market - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: FII holdings in Indian stocks have decreased to 14.7%, a fourteen-year low, as they reallocate capital towards markets with AI-driven investment narratives like Taiwan and Korea.  This shift is driven by the performance of US equities and fixed-income assets compared to India's market returns, compounded by sector-specific headwinds in IT and banking. FIIs are focusing on smaller and mid-cap companies with strong earnings growth, better governance, liquidity, and scalability, as evidenced by the rise in investable stocks and the IPO boom between 2023 and 2025.  This reallocation reflects a broader global trend of capital shifting away from emerging markets like India towards developed economies.

articles.title: Nykaa vs Honasa: Which stock should you buy after Q4 earnings? Here’s what experts say - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: FSN E-Commerce Ventures, parent company of Nykaa, reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 78 crore for the March quarter of FY26, a significant increase from Rs 20 crore in the same period last year.  Nykaa's revenue from operations rose 28% year-on-year to Rs 2,648 crore. Honasa Consumer, parent company of Mamaearth, also saw a strong rebound with a 177% jump in consolidated net profit to Rs 69 crore for the fourth quarter of FY26.  Honasa's revenue from operations surged over 23% YoY to Rs 657 crore during Q4 of FY26. Analysts believe both companies are showing strong signs of recovery, but caution against chasing short-term gains.

articles.title: Can salary-linked SIPs transform mutual fund investing for salaried Indians? Experts weigh in - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Sebi has proposed a new system for mutual fund investments through salary deductions, similar to EPF contributions. This proposal would allow employers to deduct money from employee salaries and invest it in mutual funds selected by the employees. Experts believe this could increase participation among salaried individuals, especially younger investors, but challenges remain in ensuring proper education and flexibility for first-time investors. The potential impact on monthly SIP inflows is significant, with experts predicting a steady flow of funds into mutual funds over time.  However, it is important to note that the proposal remains voluntary and will require clear operational guidelines from AMFI regarding exit options and investor education.

articles.title: HFCL shares soar 10% to fresh record high, skyrocket 172% in four months. Should you buy or wait? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: HFCL's stock price has surged over 172% in less than four months, reaching a record high of Rs 162.50 on Monday.  The surge follows a strong earnings report for the fourth quarter of FY26, with net profit and revenue significantly higher year-over-year. Harshal Dasani, Business Head at INVasset PMS, believes the stock has entered a momentum extension phase but cautions against stretched risk-reward as it may be overvalued.  The stock's future performance will depend on its ability to consolidate recent gains.

articles.title: Telangana CM exhorts SHG women to establish super markets, logistic parks and godowns - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy announced plans to support women self-help groups (SHGs) in setting up logistics parks, godowns, and super markets to address supply chain issues and empower women. The initiative aims to provide farmers with better access to markets and consumers with affordable quality goods. Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka will work with the State level bankers committee to secure financial support for these projects.  The government will provide infrastructure at nominal prices, create a corpus fund, and offer bank linkages for SHGs seeking to establish super bazaars in all 119 assembly constituencies.

articles.title: Titagarh, Jupiter Wagons shares rally up to 10% amid reports of Rs 40,000 crore order from Indian Railways - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Indian Railways is expected to issue a tender for the procurement of around 35,000-40,000 wagons annually, potentially boosting the shares of Jupiter Wagons, Titagarh Rail Systems, and Texmaco Rail.  The brokerage firm Jefferies initiated coverage on Titagarh Rail Systems with a ‘Buy’ rating and a target price of Rs 810, citing its potential to benefit from rising passenger and metro coach demand. They also highlighted the strong revenue visibility for Titagarh Rail Systems due to its large order book.  Jefferies assigned an 'Underperform' rating and a Rs 200 target price to Jupiter Wagons, while maintaining a ‘Buy’ rating on Titagarh Rail Systems.

articles.title: Melody effect: Wrong 'Parle' stock hits 5% upper circuit for 4th day, up 21% since PM Modi's gift for Meloni - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: PM Modi gifted a bag of "Melody" candies to his Italian counterpart during a recent visit, sparking viral attention. Parle Industries, the company behind the candy, shared the video on social media and highlighted its global reach.  The moment has led to a surge in Parle Products' stock price, which is now trading at an all-time high. The company, however, does not currently plan to go public.

articles.title: Why the SpaceX IPO is the talk of Wall Street and beyond | Space News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX, Elon Musk's rocket company, is preparing for a highly anticipated initial public offering (IPO) on the Nasdaq. The IPO is expected to be the largest in history and could make Musk the world's first trillionaire.  The company aims to raise upwards of $80 billion, with 23 financial institutions underwriting the deal. SpaceX will grant its founder, Elon Musk, significant control over the company post-IPO, holding 85% of voting rights. The IPO is being closely watched as a defining moment for the nascent private space industry and could potentially raise more than three times the record-breaking $25.6 billion raised by Saudi Aramco in 2019.

articles.title: PSX opens shortened trading week on bullish note; KSE-100 gains 2,300 points during intraday trade - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Stock Exchange’s (PSX) benchmark index experienced a strong opening on Monday, gaining over 2,300 points during intraday trading. The KSE-100 index rose by 1.40 percent to reach 171,438 points, fueled by hopes of a soon-to-be-announced deal between the United States and Iran regarding the Strait of Hormuz. Oil prices also declined, further contributing to positive market sentiment.

articles.title: Wipro's Rs 15,000 crore share buyback at 23% premium: Should you buy before record date? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Wipro has announced a share buyback program at Rs 250 per share, representing a 23% premium over the previous closing price. The company plans to repurchase up to 60 crore shares, or 5.7% of its total paid-up capital, for an aggregate amount not exceeding Rs 15,000 crore.  The buyback will be conducted via tender route and is expected to benefit both retail and institutional investors. The company's promoters have indicated their intention to participate in the program.

articles.title: Pakistan importing cotton from US, Brazil even before local ginning season - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's textile mills have begun importing massive amounts of cotton from the United States and Brazil, driven by a shortage of domestic supplies.  The country may spend billions of dollars on these imports this fiscal year, potentially setting a record high for import bills. The Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) is sealed due to an ownership dispute, leaving Pakistan without representation in international cotton markets. The Pakistan Cotton Ginners Association (PCGA) has proposed abolishing sales tax on cotton-related products, while the All Pakistan Textile Mills Association (APTMA) seeks reductions in energy tariffs and markup rates.  Despite these challenges, some market observers believe prices may ease after Eidul Azha holidays.

articles.title: Retail, traders chase midcap rally with stock futures bets - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: NSE reported that retail and high-net-worth individual (HNI) traders' net open positions in stock futures reached 28.57 lakh on Friday, slightly lower than Thursday's record high. Chandan Taparia, head of technical and derivatives research at Motilal Oswal Financial Services, attributed this shift to the narrow range of headline indices, limiting index trading opportunities.  Vipin Kumar, an AVP- derivatives and technical research at Globe Capital Market, also noted that retail traders are now favoring stock futures due to the lack of momentum in the indices. Despite attempts by the government to curb activity in the local futures and options market, trading volumes remain elevated.

articles.title: NFP Sampoorna Foods shares to list today. Check GMP ahead of debut - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: NFP Sampoorna Foods, a company that processes and distributes dry fruits, raised approximately Rs 24.53 crore through its IPO priced at Rs 55 per share. The IPO opened for subscription from May 18 to May 20, with allotment finalized on May 21.  The proceeds will be used for working capital requirements and general corporate purposes. Grey market premiums suggest limited listing gains despite continued activity in the SME IPO segment.

articles.title: Sun Pharma, Coforge: Indian businesses go shopping abroad as growth slows at home
articles.rephrased_article: Indian billionaires are increasingly acquiring foreign companies as domestic growth slows.  This trend, marked by high-profile deals like Sun Pharmaceuticals' $11.75 billion acquisition of Organon & Co. and Tata Motors' purchase of Iveco, reflects both strategic and operational reasons.  Experts suggest that Indian companies are seeking diversification, access to global markets, technology, and supply chain security. While the trend is driven by a desire to hedge against economic uncertainties, it also raises concerns about capital flight and potential risks associated with overseas acquisitions.

articles.title: Info Edge shares drops 4% despite 22% YoY jump in Q4 net profit; revenue up 16% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Info Edge, operator of Naukri and Jeevansathi, reported consolidated revenue of Rs 869 crore in Q4FY26, a 16% increase from the previous year. The company's standalone revenue rose 17.2% year-on-year to Rs 805 crore during the March quarter.  The board recommended a final dividend of Rs 3.60 per equity share for FY26. Hitesh Oberoi, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, stated that FY26 was a steady year with revenue growth remaining measured while operating margins improved.

articles.title: NTPC Green Energy shares fall 4% after Q4 profit drops 15% YoY - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: NTPC's renewable energy arm reported a consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 197 crore in Q4FY26, down from Rs 233 crore in the same quarter last year.  Revenue surged 47% year-on-year to Rs 913 crore, driven by strong operational growth across its clean energy portfolio. However, rising costs led to a significant increase in expenses, which contributed to the decline in profitability. Despite this, the company's PAT skyrocketed over 11 times from just Rs 17 crore in Q4FY25 and revenue climbed around 40% quarter-on-quarter.  The stock has declined around 8% over the past month.

articles.title: Petrol price crosses ₹110 mark in Bengaluru, fourth hike in 10 days - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Fuel prices in Bengaluru saw a sharp increase on May 25th, with petrol and diesel prices hiked for the fourth time in ten days. The Karnataka State Travel Operators’ Association (KSTOA) urged the government to intervene and ease the burden on the transport sector, citing increased operational costs and rising commodity prices. KSTOA president Radhakrishna Holla called for a reconsideration of fuel taxes and reduction of unnecessary government spending.

articles.title: PSX opens shortened trading week on bullish note; KSE-100 gains 2,800 points during early trade - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Stock Exchange’s (PSX) benchmark index experienced a significant surge on Monday, gaining 2,870 points to reach 170,714. This positive performance followed hopes of an imminent US-Iran deal regarding the Strait of Hormuz and was fueled by falling oil prices. The KSE-100 index rose 1.36% week-on-week, closing at 167,844.24 points, with investor sentiment boosted by improved diplomatic signals in the Middle East.

articles.title: MTAR Tech shares drop 3% after rallying 24% in 3 days. Should you buy the dip? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The share price of MTAR Tech surged to a 52-week high of Rs 8,449.50 on Friday, driven by an international order worth Rs 467.30 crore and positive FY27 growth guidance. The company's shares have experienced significant gains in recent months, with a 12% increase in one week, 55% in a month, and 233% year-to-date.  Analysts suggest buying opportunities within the range of Rs 7,500-7,700, while maintaining a stop loss at Rs 7,150.

articles.title: Govt. plans to complete paddy procurement over next 10 days: Uttam Kumar Reddy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: N. Uttam Kumar Reddy, Minister for Civil Supplies and Irrigation of Telangana, warned rice millers against deducting weight from paddy brought by farmers during the current procurement season. He emphasized that the government is committed to ensuring no farmer suffers losses due to any discrepancies in weight deductions.  He also stated that despite facing operational and financial pressures, the government aims to procure 75 lakh tonnes of paddy within the next 10 days. The Minister highlighted the unprecedented agricultural output this Rabi season, urging officials to complete procurement operations swiftly.

articles.title: Labour to expand youth work experience and training schemes | Youth unemployment | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ministers are expanding youth work experience and training schemes in response to a "quiet crisis" in youth employment. Pat McFadden, the work and pensions secretary, announced plans for 300,000 extra placements over three years, aiming to help nearly one million young people not in education, employment or training (Neet) find work.  Alan Milburn criticized the government's spending on benefits compared to support for employment, highlighting a generational crisis and increased mental health issues among young people. The expansion of sector-based work academy programs known as Swaps is expected to help reverse this trend.

articles.title: Situationer: Wheat policy failures deepen market crisis - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan national wheat sector is facing a crisis due to structural weaknesses in agricultural planning, procurement management, and food security governance.  Farmers are struggling with low prices and rising input costs, while traders are holding back stocks anticipating future shortages. The situation has escalated into a confrontation between market realities and administrative controls, prompting the Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz to order stricter stock declarations. Analysts suggest that the government's attempts to control the market through procurement have exacerbated the crisis by creating uncertainty and hindering market liquidity.  The lack of adequate reserves and inconsistent policies are further contributing to the instability in the wheat sector.

articles.title: Warren Buffett sits on $400 bn cash as Michael Burry warns of AI bubble. Is a massive market crash coming? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Berkshire Hathaway's record cash hoard of nearly $400 billion is being held back by Buffett, who believes current market conditions are not ideal for aggressive investment.  Analyst Michael Burry remains skeptical about the AI boom, citing indicators similar to the Dotcom crash. Meanwhile, South Korea and Taiwan have emerged as global stock market leaders, overtaking established Western exchanges like the UK and France. The surge in these markets is fueled by investor demand for AI-related stocks, particularly in Taiwan, where TSMC's dominance has contributed significantly to the market capitalization.

articles.title: Overseas travel spending by Indians falls to $1.09 billion in March - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Indian outward remittances for travel declined by $212.43 million to $1.09 billion in March compared to February, according to Reserve Bank of India (RBI) data.  The decline is attributed to the ongoing conflict in West Asia and Prime Minister Narendra Modi's call for reduced foreign travel. The largest portion of travel spending was allocated to "other travel" which includes holiday trips and international credit card settlements, accounting for nearly 57% of the total travel outgo at $1.09 billion.  The data also reveals a decrease in spending on education-related travel, overseas business travel, pilgrimage, and medical treatment.

articles.title: Cooling appliances’ demand surges ahead of Eidul Azha - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Despite rising living costs, appliance sales have increased in the lead-up to Eidul Azha. Sohail Malik, finance secretary of the Karachi Electronic Dealers Association (KEDA), reported a 25-30% increase in refrigerator and deep freezer sales compared to last year.  Pak Elektron (PAEL), a leading appliance manufacturer, attributes this growth to consumers' need for cooling appliances to store Qurbani meat. The company projects strong recovery in appliance sales due to economic stability, easing import restrictions, lower interest rates, and increased consumer financing.

articles.title: Squeals of horror over price caps – but how are we going to fix our broken food system? | Food & drink industry | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Treasury is asking UK supermarkets to cap price rises on essential foods in response to rising food prices, a move met with criticism from industry figures. The surge in food prices is attributed to global factors like the Iran war and a record-breaking El Niño event, highlighting vulnerabilities in the global food system.  These disruptions, coupled with climate change impacts like drought and extreme weather events, are causing significant challenges for British farmers and increasing the cost of living crisis.  The UK's reliance on imports for key resources like fertilizer and fossil gas further exacerbates these issues. The government acknowledges the need for a more resilient food system but faces resistance from market-driven approaches.

articles.title: RInfra Q4 net profit falls to Rs 918 cr; company appoints Vijesh Babu Thota as CEO - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Reliance Infrastructure reported a net profit of Rs 4,387.08 crore in the same quarter last year, but its total income fell to Rs 4,154.34 crore for the January-March period of FY26 from Rs 4,268.05 crore in the previous fiscal. Expenses increased to Rs 5,419.87 crore, driven by higher power costs, which reached Rs 3,285.68 crore. The company's annual income dropped to Rs 20,862.03 crore from Rs 23,999.29 crore in the previous fiscal year. Reliance Infrastructure appointed Vijesh Babu Thota as CEO effective May 23 and Asheesh Chaturvedi as the new CFO.

articles.title: LIC emerges as highest profit-making financial company in Jan-Mar quarter - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: LIC reported a 23% increase in net profit to Rs 23,420 crore for the fourth quarter of FY26, making it the top-performing Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE).  State Bank of India (SBI) followed with an annual profit of Rs 80,032 crore, significantly surpassing LIC's Rs 57,419 crore. Other CPSEs like Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) and Coal India also reported strong profits. Meanwhile, Vodafone Idea emerged as the highest quarterly profit earner in the January-March quarter with a record bottomline of Rs 51,970 crore.

articles.title: Treasury rejected ministers’ plan to cut VAT on public EV charging to 5% | Electric, hybrid and low-emission cars | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Government officials considered reducing the VAT charged on electricity used at public EV chargers from 20% to 5%, but the Treasury, under chancellor Rachel Reeves, rejected the proposal due to disagreements within departments. The Department for Transport supports lowering the VAT, arguing it would benefit consumers and address perceived unfairness between those with home charging options and those without.  However, the Treasury is concerned about potential lost revenue from reduced VAT, despite a London tax tribunal ruling that the rate should have been 5% all along. The government is reviewing public charging costs and plans to introduce a 3p-a-mile charge for electric cars in 2028.

articles.title: Equity MFs gain over 5% last week with international funds leading. Check top 7 with over 3% return - Weekly performers | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Equity mutual funds saw strong returns last week, with Invesco India Infrastructure Fund leading the pack at 5.70% and Nippon India Taiwan Equity Fund second at 4.36%. Other top performers included Samco Active Momentum Fund, Motilal Oswal Digital India Fund, and two international funds from Mirae Asset.  The returns ranged from 3.25% to 3.08%.

articles.title: Dividends, bonus issues: TCS, LIC, Bajaj Auto among 30 stocks turning ex-date this week. Check details - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Several Indian companies have announced record dates for upcoming corporate actions, including dividends, bonus issues, and stock splits. Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) will pay a final dividend of Rs 31 per share on June 12, while Tata Consumer Products will trade ex-dividend on Monday for its Rs 10 dividend.  LTI Mindtree, Siyaram Silk Mills, and Hatsun Agro Product have also set record dates. ITC has fixed May 27 as the record date for its final dividend, while Bajaj Auto will pay a final dividend of Rs 150 per equity share on Friday, May 29.  LIC will issue bonus shares in a 1:1 proportion on May 29, and GSK Pharma has set Friday as the record date for its final dividend.

articles.title: Naidu to inaugurate MSME Growth Summit-2026 in Vijayawada on May 25 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu will inaugurate the MSME Growth Summit-2026 in Vijayawada on Monday, May 25th. The event, a flagship initiative of the Andhra Pradesh government, aims to accelerate the growth and competitiveness of micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) across the state.  The summit will feature over 1,500 stakeholders, including entrepreneurs, industry associations, policymakers, financial institutions, and technology partners. It will showcase innovation ecosystems, infrastructure initiatives, digital transformation programs, and success stories of MSMEs from Andhra Pradesh. The summit will also launch key initiatives like the foundation stone laying for Phase III of MSME Parks, the AP Cluster Development Programme, and the SIDBI-RTIH Seed Fund.

articles.title: States to get VB-G RAM G funding based on 16th Finance Commission formula, ‘performance criteria’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Centre's new rural jobs scheme, Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (VB-G RAM G), will prioritize funding for poorer states using the 16th Finance Commission's horizontal devolution formula. The draft rules also propose allocating a portion of funds based on performance criteria such as timely wage payments and work completion rates.  The scheme, replacing the MGNREGA Act, will have a 60:40 funding split between the Centre and states and includes provisions for grievance redressal mechanisms and administrative frameworks.  Stakeholders have until June 21st to submit their feedback on the draft rules.

articles.title: Hubballi Dharwad Central MLA tells officials to facilitate export of mangoes grown in region - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: MLA Mahesh Tenginakai inaugurated the Dharwad district-level ‘Mango Mela-2026’ to support local mango farmers. The event, organized by Karnataka Agriculture Marketing Board, KCCI, and other organizations, aimed to facilitate mango exports and increase awareness about value addition.  I.G. Sanadi emphasized the importance of planting more saplings for a sustainable future. G.K. Adappagoudar highlighted the need to eliminate middlemen in the mango market.

articles.title: Petrol, diesel prices hiked again in Bengaluru; transport sector warns of ripple effect - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Oil marketing companies raised petrol and diesel prices in Bengaluru for the third time this month, increasing prices by an average of 90 paise per litre. This latest increase has added to concerns about rising inflation and its impact on commuters, transport operators, businesses, and consumers.  The president of the Karnataka State Travel Owners’ Association, K. Radhakrishna Holla, called for immediate government intervention to reduce fuel taxes and provide relief measures for the transportation sector. Ride-hailing cab drivers in Bengaluru also expressed concern over the impact on their earnings, while consumers reported that the price hikes were affecting grocery expenses.

articles.title: Power cuts caused by load issues, not shortage, says Minister R. Nirmalkumar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Minister for Energy Resources and Law R. Nirmalkumar stated that recent power cuts in Chennai and other districts were due to increased demand during the summer, not a shortage of supply. Mr. Nirmalkumar explained that the Electricity Department is addressing issues with load management, rapid response teams, and call centers to resolve complaints promptly. The department faces financial distress and is implementing reforms to improve efficiency and address outstanding debt.

articles.title: ₹350 crore investment to generate 2,300 employment opportunities in Bihar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bihar Industrial Area Development Authority (BIADA) approved 20 industrial projects during a meeting chaired by Secretary, Industries Department and MD of BIADA, Kundan Kumar. The projects are expected to attract investments worth ₹350 crore and create employment opportunities for 2,300 people.  Industries Minister Shreyasi Singh highlighted the government's commitment to developing an investor-friendly environment and establishing Bihar as a modern industrial hub.

articles.title: Fuel price hike: Bengaluru hoteliers feel the heat - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Fuel prices have increased for the third time in 10 days, raising concerns about their impact on transportation and logistics sectors. Hotels in Bengaluru are warning that rising costs will force them to increase menu prices or face financial strain.  The industry is already struggling with high commercial LPG cylinder prices and supply shortages, making it difficult to absorb the increased fuel costs without impacting consumers.

articles.title: Traders’ coalition demands turnover tax be reduced to 0.5pc - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Traders’ coalition in Pakistan, represented by the All Pakistan Anjuman-i-Tajiran and Traders Action Committee, demanded a reduction in the turnover tax rate to 0.5% ahead of the upcoming federal budget. They praised the efforts of Prime Minister's Adviser on Finance Bilal Azhar Kiani for introducing reforms in tax collection but criticized the use of forceful tax collection methods and alleged corruption within the Point of Sale (POS) system. The coalition also called for investigations into FBR officers’ assets, a review of confiscated vehicles by customs authorities, and special tax exemptions for provinces affected by terrorism.

articles.title: Agri-tech has improved productivity and post-harvest management, say experts at webinar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Experts at a webinar organized by SRM Institute of Science and Technology and The Hindu discussed the advancements in agricultural technology.  Dr. Devinder Dhingra, Principal Scientist (Process Engineering), ICAR, highlighted that 47% of farm work is now mechanized, leading to surplus production and exports. Poorna Pushkala, CEO of Samunnati Foundation, emphasized the role of decentralised energy systems and ad-tech innovations in bolstering the sector.  Leenus Jesu Martin M., Dean of SRMIST's Faculty of Engineering and Technology, noted that agriculture is now a multi-disciplinary field with contributions from mechanical, automation, and computing engineers.

articles.title: Rising global costs threaten Mexico’s production costs and food stability | Inflation | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Rising global costs of fuel and fertilizer, driven by shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, are forcing Mexican consumers to tighten budgets and cut back on consumption.  The price hikes for staples like tomatoes, potatoes, beef, and chillies have led to increased consumer spending on food and a drop in sales at local markets.  Elites, including Elvira Pasillas, professor at the Western Institute of Technology and Higher Education (ITESO), are concerned about the impact this will have on low-income households who spend nearly 70 percent of their earnings on food. The rising cost of fuel, roadblocks, and extortion by organized criminal groups are also contributing to higher prices for meat, produce, and other goods.  The Mexican government has implemented a voluntary agreement with retailers to reduce the fuel tax but this is expected to strain public finances.

articles.title: Death toll jumps to 90 in China coal mine blast - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: A gas explosion at the Liushenyu coal mine in Qinyuan county, China, injured 247 workers and resulted in a significant loss of life. Chinese President Xi Jinping and Premier Li Qiang ordered immediate rescue efforts and investigations into the cause of the accident.  The death toll has risen from initial reports of eight to over 20 dead, with authorities detaining executives of the mine's operator. Rescue operations are ongoing.

articles.title: Bandhan Small Cap among top 5 smallcap funds with highest risk-adjusted returns. Check details - Risk adjusted returns | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Bandhan Small Cap Fund, ITI Small Cap Fund, and Aditya Birla Sun Life Smallcap 50 Index Fund topped the list of India's top-performing small-cap funds based on Sharpe ratio, a risk-adjusted return measure.  The Bandhan Small Cap Fund led with a 1.17 Sharpe ratio over the past three years, followed by ITI Small Cap Fund (1.02) and Aditya Birla Sun Life Smallcap 50 Index Fund (0.84). Kotak Nifty Smallcap 50 Index Fund and Invesco India Smallcap Fund also performed well with Sharpe ratios of 0.84 and 0.98 respectively.

articles.title: June quarter earnings to determine market direction, says Sunil Subramaniam, warns on risks in near term - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Subramaniam, a financial expert, believes the recent rally in pharmaceuticals stocks was partly due to rupee depreciation and export-oriented companies. However, he cautions against extrapolating current quarterly earnings into the future as they don't fully reflect higher input costs. He expects consumer durables to outperform FMCG companies in the near term due to strong demand for products like air conditioners and refrigerators.  He also favors public sector banks over private lenders and believes the June quarter earnings season will be crucial in determining market direction.

articles.title: Government plans to inaugurate Bhogapuram Airport on July 5: MP - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M. Sribharat, an MP, announced that the State government plans to inaugurate the International Airport at Bhogapuram on July 5th with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.  He expressed confidence that several airlines would soon begin operations from the new airport following its inauguration. Scoot Airlines will commence international services from Bhogapuram Airport starting July 8th.

articles.title: Bitcoin faces fresh selling pressure despite U.S.-Iran easing; over $400 million liquidated in 1 day - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Bitcoin and Ethereum experienced weekly declines, falling 4.31% and 7.15%, respectively, due to global macroeconomic concerns like rising Treasury yields and persistent inflation. The broader risk-off environment led to outflows from crypto investment products, with Bitcoin funds accounting for the majority of withdrawals.  Piyush Walke, a Derivatives Research Analyst at Delta Exchange, stated that easing U.S.-Iran tensions failed to revive sentiment in the market, while continued outflows from Bitcoin ETFs and profit-taking after a U.S. Senate crypto bill breakthrough kept pressure on digital assets.

articles.title: Gokaldas Exports posts 9% sequential rise in Q4 revenue - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Gokaldas Exports reported a lower profit for the fiscal year 2026 compared to the previous year, despite a 9% quarter-on-quarter increase in total income. The company attributed this growth to a recovery in its Africa business and steady performance in India, despite tariff disruptions. Sivaramakrishnan Ganapathi, vice chairman and managing director of Gokaldas Exports, highlighted the impact of US tariffs and geopolitical events on costs and margins, but emphasized the company's resilience and strong customer relationships.

articles.title: NTPC Q4 Results: Cons PAT jumps 34% YoY to Rs 10,615 crore; Rs 3.5/share dividend announced - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The state-run power company's board recommended a final dividend of Rs 3.50 per share for the financial year 2025-26, subject to shareholder approval at the upcoming AGM. The company reported a significant increase in PAT (profit after tax) and revenue during Q4FY26, with revenues reaching Rs 48,548 crore compared to Rs 44,658 crore in Q3FY26.  The company's expenses also increased by 9% on a quarter-on-quarter basis but declined by 0.35% year-on-year.

articles.title: Bandhan Small Cap among top 5 smallcap funds with highest risk-adjusted returns. Check details - Risk adjusted returns | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Bandhan Small Cap Fund, ITI Small Cap Fund, and Aditya Birla Sun Life Smallcap 50 Index Fund were among the top performers in terms of Sharpe ratio, with returns exceeding risk-free rates.  The Bandhan Small Cap Fund led the pack with a ratio of 1.17 over the past three years, followed by ITI Small Cap Fund at 1.02 and Aditya Birla Sun Life Smallcap 50 Index Fund at 0.84.  Kotak Nifty Smallcap 50 Index Fund and Invesco India Smallcap Fund also showed positive returns with Sharpe ratios of 0.84 and 0.98 respectively.

articles.title: Planning to take international exposure for three years? Here are top 5 global funds with over 40% gain - International gains | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nippon India Taiwan Equity Fund, Mirae Asset NYSE FANG+ ETF FoF, and DSP World Gold Mining Overseas Equity Omni FoF were among the top-performing funds in the last three years, according to MF Screener.  The Nippon India Taiwan Equity Fund led with a 64.14% return over three years, followed by Mirae Asset NYSE FANG+ ETF FoF at 51.09%.  Other top performers include DSP World Gold Mining Overseas Equity Omni FoF, and Motilal Oswal Nasdaq 100 FoF.

articles.title: PPFAS Mutual Fund introduces choti SIP in Parag Parikh Flexi Cap, Large Cap and 3 other schemes - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Parag Parikh Mutual Fund has introduced a new "Choti SIP" facility for its five equity funds, allowing first-time investors to invest in mutual funds with a minimum of Rs 250 per installment.  The fund house also announced changes to the Systematic Transfer Plan (STP) processing frequency, effective May 21, 2026, to only process on business days. The changes are part of an addendum to the Statement of Additional Information (SAI) and Scheme Information Documents (SIDs) for the affected schemes.

articles.title: Nifty stays range-bound as resistance near 23,800 caps upside move - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The India VIX cooled off, declining 4.68% to 17.91 for the week. The Nifty index closed with a net gain of 75.80 points (+0.32%), but remains below a crucial resistance zone near 23,800-23,850.  While recent volatility has stabilized, traders should monitor the index's behavior near this level and avoid aggressive buying until it decisively breaks above. The Nifty Metal Index is showing relative strength, while other sectors like Midcap 100 and Energy are also performing well.

articles.title: Govt reduces petrol, high-speed diesel prices by Rs6 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The government reduced the price of petrol by Rs6 per litre and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs6.80 on Friday, bringing the price of petrol to Rs403.78 per litre and HSD to Rs402.78. The Petroleum Division announced the new prices would be effective from May 23rd, marking the second consecutive week of fuel price reductions.  This decision comes after a period of fluctuating prices following the US-Israeli war on Iran in February. The government has been adjusting petroleum prices weekly since then, aiming to balance global market fluctuations and domestic needs.

articles.title: FIIs sell over Rs 30K crore worth of Indian equities in May as outflows swell to Rs 2.22 lakh crore. What lies ahead? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) sold domestic shares worth Rs 4,440.47 crore on Friday while domestic institutional investors (DIIs) were net buyers at Rs 6,003.53 crore. This helped the benchmark indices close with gains despite strong selling pressure in pharma and health stocks.  Pabitro Mukherjee, Associate Vice President - Research at Bajaj Broking, noted that investor sentiment remains cautious due to geopolitical tensions and rising interest rates. He added that institutional activity is expected to be driven by global developments, particularly US-Iran negotiations.

articles.title: Vedanta, MCX, among 10 stocks that saw highest increase in retail shareholding in Q4. Do you own any? - Retail Rise | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Vedanta, MCX, and other companies saw significant increases in retail shareholding during the March 2026 quarter.  The stocks, including Hitachi Energy India, NALCO, Acutaas Chemicals, Tata Steel, ONGC, GE Vernova T&D India, Bharat Forge, and Sterlite Technologies, saw their retail holdings rise due to heightened market volatility driven by global events. MCX also experienced a notable increase in retail holding value, reflecting investor confidence in the domestic stock market.

articles.title: Reliance Industries, TCS, among 10 stocks with sharpest decrease in retail shareholding in Q4 - Retail holding decline | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Rising oil prices and geopolitical tensions in the Iran war have contributed to a decline in investor confidence, leading to decreased retail holdings across several Indian companies.  HDFC Bank, Reliance Industries, ITC, Larsen & Toubro, Tata Consultancy Services, Infosys, Jio Financial Services, Hindustan Unilever, and Asian Paints all saw significant drops in retail shareholding during the March quarter, with some stocks experiencing declines of over 20%.  This trend reflects a broader market sentiment of caution as investors grapple with rising inflation and potential interest rate hikes.

articles.title: World’s most powerful economies by 2030: Prediction reveals future global leaders | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: By 2030, several emerging economies are projected to rise in global GDP rankings, while established industrial powers may experience slight declines. China is expected to remain the world's largest economy by purchasing power parity measures, driven by its manufacturing scale and increasing focus on technology, infrastructure investment, and consumer spending. The United States, despite competition from Asia, is predicted to maintain a top tier position due to financial markets, research institutions, multinational companies, and the continued influence of the US dollar.  India, Japan, Germany, Russia, Indonesia, Brazil, United Kingdom, and France are also expected to remain influential in the global economy.

articles.title: Nomura picks 6 stocks with up to 49% upside potential that can benefit from India’s EV push - EV Boost | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nomura, an international brokerage, predicts a surge in India's electric vehicle (EV) adoption due to government policies and rising fuel prices. The brokerage recommends six stocks likely to benefit from this trend: Mahindra & Mahindra, Hyundai Motor India, TVS Motors, Ather Energy, Sona BLW Precision Forgings, and UNO Minda. These companies are expected to see significant growth in the near future, with potential upside ranging from 20% to 49%.

articles.title: Reeves’s tax cut on children’s meals a political ‘soundbite’, say restaurateurs | Tax and spending | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Rachel Reeves, the chancellor, announced a temporary reduction in VAT on children’s meals in restaurants from 20% to 5% between June and September. Will Murray, owner of London restaurant Fallow, and Tim Martin, founder and chair of Wetherspoons, have expressed skepticism about the impact of the measure, arguing that it won't make a significant difference for families or businesses.  UKHospitality, the lobbying group for the industry, has called for a permanent reduction in VAT for the entire hospitality sector to bring the UK in line with European rates.

articles.title: Contrarian Tactics: How to survive market volatility and generate steady returns - Investing approach | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Michael Price, a renowned investing legend, advises investors to adopt a curious and analytical mindset when evaluating stocks. He suggests considering not only the current market value but also the potential acquisition price by other investors. Price recommends allocating two-thirds of a portfolio to value stocks and dedicating the remaining one-third to special situation instruments like arbitrage and distressed securities.  He cautions against blindly following market trends and emphasizes that investors should focus on opportunities others may overlook, such as mispriced assets.

articles.title: Oil prices settle higher on slow progress in US-Iran peace talks - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Brent and WTI crude oil futures experienced gains on Friday, driven by shifting expectations for a peace deal between Iran and the U.S.  Diplomatic sources indicated progress in talks, with Pakistan's army chief traveling to Iran, while U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressed optimism about potential resolution. However, uncertainties remain regarding Iran's uranium stockpile and control over the Strait of Hormuz, and global oil inventories continue to deplete due to reduced oil flows through the strait.  Analysts predict a modest increase in July production by OPEC+ members, but full oil flow through the strait is not expected until the first or second quarter of 2027.

articles.title: Dollar near six-week high amid Iran war jitters - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's foreign minister met with Pakistan's interior minister to discuss proposals for ending the U.S.-Israeli conflict, according to Iranian media reports.  Traders are concerned about ongoing energy disruptions and their impact on consumer prices, potentially forcing a tighter monetary policy response from the Federal Reserve. The dollar index rose slightly while the yen weakened against the greenback as rising oil prices and persistent inflation pressures continue to affect global markets.

articles.title: Planning SIPs for a car or house in 10 years? Experts recommend diversified equity funds for long-term goals - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Pankaj Mathpal, MD of Optima Money Managers, advised viewers seeking to invest through SIPs with a 10-year horizon to consider diversified equity funds like ICICI Prudential Midcap Fund, Motilal Oswal Large and Midcap Fund, Bajaj Finserv Flexicap Fund, and HDFC Midcap Fund. He cautioned against investing in gold ETFs due to the government's efforts to reduce gold imports and recommended a focus on diversified mutual funds and multi-asset allocation funds for risk management. Mathpal also warned against excessive exposure to thematic or sectoral funds without understanding market cycles and emphasized that investors with limited knowledge should stick to these strategies.

articles.title: Paytm block deal: SocGen, Ghisallo, Viridian among biggest buyers in Rs 964 crore stake sale - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Societe Generale, Ghisallo Master Fund LP, and Viridian Asia Opportunities Master Fund were among the largest buyers in a recent transaction of Paytm shares, totaling approximately Rs 964 crore.
