Domestic institutional investors such as Nippon India Mutual Fund and Sundaram Mutual Fund also participated in the deal. The stock closed down on Friday by 3.74%, settling at Rs 1,112.40 after a year of strong gains driven by improved operational metrics and investor confidence.  Global investment bank Citigroup Global Markets Mauritius is reported to have been appointed as the placement agent for the transaction.

articles.title: For every job at Mazagon Dock, 6.4 jobs are created across economy: Captain Jagmohan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Captain Jagmohan (Retd.), Chairman and Managing Director of Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL), stated that one direct job at MDL generates six and a half jobs across India. He cited the Project 17A frigate as an example, where 4,500 MDL workers support nearly 28,000 positions in ancillary industries. The Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision (MAKV) aims to place India among the top five shipbuilding countries by 2047 with a target of 4.5 million gross tonnage and an expected investment of ₹4.5 lakh crore.

articles.title: US jury finds Boeing not guilty in 737 MAX grounding lawsuit - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: A US jury ruled in favor of Boeing, finding the aerospace giant not liable for lost revenue claims from Polish airline LOT. LOT had accused Boeing of fraud and sought $250 million in compensation for alleged false representations concerning its 737 MAX jets, which were grounded for 20 months following two deadly crashes.  The jury's decision comes after a series of lawsuits related to the MAX crashes, including settlements with victim families and a criminal charge dismissal against Boeing as part of an agreement with US prosecutors.

articles.title: Wall Street Week Ahead: Soaring stocks could face rocky patch as earnings wind down, yields perk up - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The S&P 500 remains relatively stable despite recent market volatility.  While earnings season has concluded, investors are now focusing on macroeconomic factors like rising bond yields and inflation concerns. These factors have raised the possibility of interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve. The upcoming release of the April personal consumption expenditures price index will provide further insight into inflationary pressures. Key retailers including Costco, Best Buy, and Dollar Tree will report their earnings in the coming week, offering clues about consumer spending patterns amid elevated gas prices.  The performance of companies like Nvidia, which has seen strong AI-related revenue growth, is also being closely watched.

articles.title: Retail players can skip Central Bank of India OFS, say analysts, cite margin and earnings concerns - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Centre is selling up to an 8% stake in the State Bank of India (SBI) through an initial public offering (OFS).  Investors are advised to avoid participating due to concerns about profitability and a potential supply overhang. The retail portion of the OFS opens on Monday, with the floor price set at ₹31 per share, a discount of 8.6% from Thursday's closing price. Analysts suggest caution as further stake sales may be necessary to meet public shareholding requirements.

articles.title: D-Street ends week in the green with war and peace on its mind - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The NSE Nifty 50 and BSE Sensex both closed higher on Friday, rising 0.3% each to close at 23,719.30 and 75,415.35 respectively.  Analysts predict a potential breakout for the Nifty, which could reach 25,800 levels in the coming month. While foreign portfolio investors sold shares worth ₹4,440.5 crore on Friday, domestic institutional investors bought shares worth ₹6,003.5 crore. The India VIX volatility index dropped 4.7% this week, indicating a positive short-term outlook for the market.

articles.title: Patient capital trusts India as hot money exits; FDI inflow rises 17% YoY - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Gross foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows increased to $94.5 billion in 2025-26 from $80.6 billion the previous year, while net FDI inflows surged to $7.7 billion from $1 billion.  The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) attributed this growth to greenfield investments in finance and technology sectors, despite a moderation in gross inflows. External commercial borrowings also decreased to $43 billion in 2025-26. The RBI noted continued pressure from foreign portfolio investor (FPI) outflows.

articles.title: Kevin Warsh sworn in as Fed chair as Trump faces backlash over economy | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kevin Warsh, hand-picked by Donald Trump, was sworn in as chair of the US Federal Reserve, tasked with navigating an uncertain economic outlook.  Warsh faces pressure to cut interest rates despite rising inflation and criticism over his perceived lack of independence from the president.  The new Fed chair pledged a "reform-oriented" approach while acknowledging challenges facing the economy. Public opinion polls show growing dissatisfaction with Trump's economic record, particularly regarding immigration enforcement and affordability issues. The US Federal Reserve faces mounting pressure to address these concerns as Americans grapple with rising fuel prices and inflation.

articles.title: Rajasthan Cabinet approves new industrial development policy with focus on talent economy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Rajasthan Cabinet approved a new industrial development policy focused on talent economy and private sector participation to create a world-class industrial infrastructure.  Industries and Commerce Minister Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore stated the policy would provide incentives for micro, small, and medium enterprises, one district one product, and the export sector. The policy aims to boost the state's economy to $350 billion by 2028-29.  The Cabinet also approved decisions on energy production, water conservation, and pensioners' welfare.

articles.title: Uk Airlines Offers: UK airlines EasyJet and Jet2 assure holidaymakers: No extra charges for summer flights despite rising fuel costs | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: easyJet and Jet2 have assured customers that their summer travel plans remain unaffected despite rising jet fuel prices linked to Middle Eastern tensions.  Both airlines stated they had no fuel shortages and would not introduce extra charges for flights or package holidays. However, Kenton Jarvis, chief executive of easyJet, warned that higher oil prices could eventually affect fares later in the summer. Willie Walsh, director general of the International Air Transport Association, cautioned that airlines may have to pass on rising fuel costs to passengers.

articles.title: Vadodara to host Vibrant Gujarat Regional Conference in June - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Vibrant Gujarat Regional Conference (VGRC) will be held in Vadodara in the last week of June 2026, focusing on Central Gujarat's industrial strength and investment opportunities. The conference aims to highlight the region's contributions to manufacturing, including its dominance in sectors like transport equipment, auto components, pharmaceuticals, and beverages.  The event will attract stakeholders from industry, government, and academia, with a focus on tourism and culture. Gujarat is expected to showcase its strengths in these areas, including heritage sites like Sabarmati Ashram and the Statue of Unity.

articles.title: Power Division warns consumers against fake subsidy links, QR code scams - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Ministry of Energy’s Power Division issued a warning to consumers about fraudulent activities targeting electricity bill subsidies. The Power Division advised against clicking on suspicious links or QR codes, as criminals are attempting to steal personal information through these methods.  Consumers were urged not to share any personal details for obtaining subsidies and law enforcement agencies have been informed of the scam.

articles.title: Why thousands of stock trades tied to Trump are raising eyebrows
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump's name appears on government filings revealing thousands of stock trades made in the first three months of this year. The Trump Organization stated that neither the president, his family, nor the company were involved in selecting or approving investments and receive no advance notice of trading activity.

articles.title: Lucky Motors partners with China's GAC as it bets fuel shock will drive EV switch - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Lucky Motors, a Pakistani conglomerate, is launching EVs in partnership with Guangzhou Automobile Group (GAC) and plans local assembly by December 2026.  The move comes amid rising fuel prices and increased interest in solar energy, which the company believes will accelerate EV adoption. The CEO of Lucky Motors, Muhammad Faisal, expects initial imported stock to sell out quickly.  Lucky Motors, which also assembles smartphones, is exploring local battery manufacturing and plans to export Pakistani-assembled vehicles to other right-hand drive markets.

articles.title: Mumbai, Maharashtra emerging as key hubs for global investment and clean energy partnerships, say diplomats - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Consul Generals from Australia and Finland highlighted the growing investment opportunities in Mumbai and Maharashtra, emphasizing infrastructure development, clean energy, education, and technology sectors.  They praised Mumbai's transformation, citing projects like the Coastal Road and metro expansion as drivers of investor confidence. Both diplomats acknowledged challenges faced by foreign investors, including regulatory clarity and streamlined approval systems. Despite these challenges, they expressed optimism about Mumbai's long-term trajectory as a global economic hub.

articles.title: Infrastructure is foundation of economic growth, says M. Jamshed - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M. Jamshed, during a special address at The Hindu’s Maharashtra Infrastructure Conclave 2026, highlighted the crucial role of infrastructure in development, emphasizing its importance for India's economic growth. He praised Maharashtra as a leading example of infrastructure development from Delhi's perspective and expressed optimism about the state's continued success.  Mr. Jamshed noted that the Centre's focus on integrated infrastructure development since 2014 has expanded beyond traditional sectors, encompassing physical, digital, and social infrastructure. He emphasized core sectors like roads, railways, maritime transport, and energy alongside digital and social infrastructure segments such as rural drinking water, sanitation, and water resource management.

articles.title: US stocks today: Dow hits record high as Middle East hopes lift sentiment and Warsh takes Fed charge - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The S&P 500 closed at a new high, marking its eighth consecutive weekly gain.  Semiconductor stocks were mostly higher, driven by gains in Qualcomm and Lenovo Group's strong quarterly results. The Federal Reserve welcomed new Chair Kevin Warsh, while Estee Lauder rose after ending merger talks with Puig.   The U.S. made progress toward a deal with Iran, though more work remains according to Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

articles.title: Colgate-Palmolive India Q4 profit down marginally to Rs 353 cr; FY26 revenue dips to Rs 6,124 cr - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Colgate-Palmolive India Ltd (CPIL) reported a 9% year-on-year increase in net profit after tax, excluding one-offs and exceptional items, to Rs 355 crore for the March quarter of FY26. Sales also rose by 9%, reaching Rs 1,582.77 crore. CPIL's Managing Director & CEO Prabha Narasimhan highlighted the company's focus on premiumization and driving consumption, which contributed to the growth. The company's total income increased by 8.8% to Rs 1,612.22 crore for the quarter.  The company declared a second interim dividend of Rs 24 per share.

articles.title: Ahead of kharif season, Dharwad Deputy Commissioner warns traders of strict action ‘creating artificial scarcity’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Deputy Commissioner Snehal R. of Dharwad district held a video conference with officials, seed and fertilizer dealers, and farmer leaders to address concerns about the upcoming monsoon season and ensure timely availability of seeds and fertilizer. Ms. Snehal warned against unfair trade practices and directed officials to monitor market conditions, set up vigilance squads, and report on seed and fertilizer availability.  She assured farmers that sufficient quantities of seeds and fertilizer were available in Dharwad for the kharif season and urged them to purchase from authorized sources like Raitha Samparka Kendras and fertilizer sale centres.

articles.title: Kevin Warsh takes over US Fed with a policy problem already in view - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Federal Reserve's new chair, Jerome Powell, faces a challenging task as he navigates the complex economic landscape.  Christopher Waller, a Fed Governor who has recently shifted his stance on monetary policy, is advocating for a possible rate hike to combat rising inflation. The debate over policy is intensifying, with Powell facing pressure from colleagues and market sentiment that favors tighter monetary policy. Powell will need to weigh the impact of his decisions on both inflation and maximum employment, while also navigating potential conflicts with the Trump administration's economic agenda.  The Fed's next meeting on June 16-17 will be crucial as they vote on interest rates and new economic projections.

articles.title: BSE 100 rejig: Paytm, Ashok Leyland and CG Power enter index; Adani Group-owned Ambuja, 2 more exit - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The BSE Index Services announced changes to the BSE Sensex and BSE Sensex Next 50 indices, effective today.  Ambuja Cements, Tube Investments, Paytm, Ashok Leyland, and CG Power were among companies that saw significant shifts in their positions within these indexes. The additions of TVS Motor Company, Ashok Leyland, One 97 Communications, and CG Power and Industrial Solutions to the BSE Sensex Next 50 are notable changes ahead of its implementation on June 22, 2026.

articles.title: KERC directs Escoms to give consumers 15 clear days to pay bills - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka Electricity Regulatory Commission (KERC) has mandated that all electricity distribution companies provide consumers with a minimum of 15 days to pay their bills from the actual bill issuance date, not the scheduled billing date. The order, effective June 1st, requires all bills to clearly state the generation date and time, and mandates payment due dates be calculated accordingly.  The commission emphasized that late or extended billing cycles do not exempt Escoms from providing consumers with sufficient payment time.

articles.title: Govt reduces petrol by Rs6 per litre, high-speed diesel by Rs6.8 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The government reduced the price of petrol by Rs6 per litre and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs6.80 on Friday, bringing the new prices to Rs403.78 per litre for petrol and Rs402.78 per litre for HSD. This is the second consecutive week of fuel price reductions, following a series of adjustments made in response to global market fluctuations and the ongoing US-Israeli war on Iran. The government has been adjusting petroleum prices weekly since the conflict began, aiming to mitigate its impact on consumers while balancing budgetary considerations.

articles.title: NTPC Green Energy Q4 Results: Cons PAT declines 15% YoY to Rs 197 crore despite 47% revenue uptick - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Despite a 47% revenue growth to Rs 913 crore in Q4FY26, the state-run company saw its profit fall to Rs 247 crore from Rs 307 crore in the same period last year. The decline was attributed to a sharp rise in expenses, which increased by 60% to Rs 713 crore, driven by factors like employee benefits and finance costs.  However, PAT surged multi-fold sequentially, reaching Rs 247 crore from Rs 17 crore in Q3FY26.

articles.title: Kevin Warsh sworn in as new US Fed chair | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.sentiment_target: United States Federal Reserve Board of Governors
articles.rephrased_article: Kevin Warsh was sworn in as the new chair of the United States Federal Reserve Board of Governors, succeeding Jerome Powell.  Warsh's appointment comes amid political pressure on the historically non-partisan institution and a contentious nomination process.  He will lead the central bank at a time when inflation is rising, with consumer prices increasing 0.6 percent in April and energy prices surging.  The first policy meeting Warsh will lead is scheduled for June 16-17.

articles.title: Sebi bars seven entities in social media stock recommendations, alleges Rs 58 crore gains - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sebi, India's market regulator, has accused seven individuals and a group of entities, including Rohan Gupta and Sharon Gupta, of manipulating stock prices through social media influence. The regulator conducted searches between January 21-24, 2026, after observing unusual trading patterns linked to the group's online activity. Sebi alleges that the group accumulated shares before recommending them on social media platforms, profiting from price increases following retail investor participation in those stocks.  The regulator found a significant increase in trade value and profits for the group during the examination period.

articles.title: Deepa Jewellers, Cotec Healthcare receive Sebi approval for IPOs - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Deepa Jewellers, a Hyderabad-based company specializing in hallmarked gold jewelry processing and trading, plans to raise funds through an IPO consisting of a fresh issue and offer-for-sale. The IPO will include up to Rs 250 crore worth of shares from the company and up to 1.18 crore shares offered for sale by promoters Ashish Agarwal and Seema Agarwal.  Cotec Healthcare, a contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) serving pharmaceutical companies, also received Sebi approval for its IPO. The company manufactures formulations across various therapeutic segments and operates a manufacturing facility in Roorkee with an installed capacity of over 4 billion units.

articles.title: LTM to acquire Randstad’s tech, consulting businesses for €160 million - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: LTM, formerly LTIMindtree, has proposed to acquire Randstad's Technology and Consulting Services business in several European countries for €160 million. The acquisition, expected to be completed by Q3 of fiscal 2027, aims to expand LTM’s presence in key markets and provide local expertise in digital engineering, cybersecurity, and IoT.  The deal also includes a five-year IT services partnership with Randstad's India Global Capability Center and a strategic talent MSP for LTM's expanding global workforce.

articles.title: Estée Lauder ends merger talks with Gaultier owner Puig | Retail industry | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Estée Lauder and its Spanish rival Puig have ended merger talks that would have created a $40 billion beauty group. The talks stalled over disagreements about the compensation demanded by Charlotte Tilbury, a key brand owned by Puig.  The termination of the discussions was welcomed by Estée Lauder investors, whose shares rose after the news.

articles.title: Arvind Panagariya’s advice to RBI: ‘100 is just a number; let rupee depreciate or reserves will bleed out’ - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The 16th Finance Commission Chairman, Panagariya, urged the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) not to be swayed by the psychological impact of the Rs 100-per-dollar mark when formulating policy decisions. He argued that a depreciation in the rupee is the appropriate response to current oil price fluctuations, regardless of their duration.  He cautioned against relying on temporary measures like dollar-denominated sovereign bonds or high-interest NRI deposits to support the currency and warned that artificially defending the rupee would deplete foreign exchange reserves.

articles.title: Australian government plans for ‘worst-case scenario’ retail fuel rationing, documents reveal | Energy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Australian government has outlined plans for retail fuel rationing as the International Energy Agency warns of an impending oil market crisis. The federal energy minister, Chris Bowen, can declare a liquid fuel emergency (LFE) and implement rationing measures under the Liquid Fuels Emergency Act if industry-led solutions prove inadequate.  While the government initially ruled out the need for rationing, documents reveal discussions about potential rationing scenarios, including limiting purchase amounts per vehicle.

articles.title: Oil prices rise as investors doubt breakthrough in US-Iran peace talks - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Oil prices rose on Friday but were still headed for a weekly loss as investors remained cautious about the prospects of a US-Iran peace deal. Brent crude futures increased by $1.66, or 1.6%, to $104.24 a barrel while US West Texas Intermediate futures rose by $1.11, or 1.2%, at $97.46.  Analysts predict that oil prices will remain elevated due to supply disruptions caused by the war in Ukraine and concerns about global economic growth.

articles.title: Standard Chartered boss apologises for ‘lower-value human capital’ comments amid job cuts | Standard Chartered | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Standard Chartered chief executive Bill Winters apologized for using the term "lower-value human capital" to describe employees facing job losses due to artificial intelligence.  Winters, in a series of posts on LinkedIn, attempted to clarify his comments about automation and employee transition but faced criticism for his choice of words. The bank plans to cut 15% of its back-office roles by 2030, impacting employees in several locations.

articles.title: Markets to enter prolonged “drag phase,” not deep correction: Vikas Khemani - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Khemani, managing director of a prominent investment firm, stated that while corporate earnings have held up well, the full impact of global disruptions like the war in Ukraine is yet to be seen. He believes markets are prepared for these impacts and do not expect significant earnings growth in Q1.  He remains optimistic about India's domestic growth story, citing strong consumer demand and a resilient investment cycle. Khemani advises investors to focus on bottom-up stock selection rather than broad market trends, highlighting opportunities in manufacturing, pharma, CDMO, BFSI, and IT. He cautions against chasing FOMO and emphasizes the importance of long-term diversification strategies based on individual goals.

articles.title: Bank Nifty near key resistance zone; breakout above 54,300 crucial: Ajit Mishra - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nifty has been consolidating for the second week, with upside capped near 24,000.  Bank Nifty has shown stronger performance, gaining around 1 percent and approaching the 54,300–54,350 resistance zone. Ajit Mishra, a market analyst, suggests traders focus on defined-risk strategies like bull call spreads in both indices due to the expiry week. He also highlights opportunities across sectors, including IT, pharma, healthcare, energy, and auto, with specific stocks like Angel One and Trent showing potential for further gains.

articles.title: Picked wrong Melody? Parle Industries shares hit 5% upper circuit for 3rd day - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: During a visit to Italy, Prime Minister Narendra Modi gifted Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni a bag of candies called "Melody." The viral video of the exchange sparked interest in Indian brands and led to marketing campaigns by companies like Air India.  The candy's maker, Parle Products, confirmed it is exported to 100 countries. While Parle Industries shares saw a significant jump following the incident, the company has no immediate plans for an initial public offering.

articles.title: 38.5% drop in H-1B registrations for FY 2027: Immigration attorney says numbers were like this 10 years ago - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The USCIS released the details of the H-1B FY 2027 lottery, reporting a 38.5% drop in registrations compared to the previous year.  The agency attributed this decline to President Donald Trump's America First policies and emphasized the shift towards prioritizing highly skilled foreign workers with advanced degrees and higher salaries. The new wage-based selection system saw an increase in applicants with advanced degrees, leading to a 71.5% representation of selected aliens holding a U.S. master’s degree or higher.  Immigration attorney Emily Neumann suggests that the drop is largely due to the $100,000 fee imposed by Trump on applications from outside the United States.

articles.title: MTAR Tech shares soar 24% in just three sessions. What’s triggering this renewed buying spree? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: MTAR Technologies, a Hyderabad-based precision engineering company, secured a new order worth Rs 467.30 crore from an international company, continuing its strong business momentum. This follows the company's recent announcement of a Rs 2,279 crore order from another international client.  The company has revised its FY27 revenue growth guidance upward to more than 80% and expects margins of around 24%. MTAR Technologies also reported strong financial results for FY26 with a net profit increase of nearly 78%, driven by higher product sales and robust order book execution.

articles.title: ITC has paid dividends worth Rs 90 per share since 2020. Should you buy? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: ITC announced a significant dividend payout of Rs 14.50 per share for FY26, marking its largest dividend in nearly six years. The FMCG company's total dividend payout for the fiscal year stands at Rs 14.50 per share with a face value of Re 1 each. Shareholders will receive the dividend between July 24 and 29, contingent upon approval from shareholders at the upcoming Annual General Meeting on July 23rd. The company also reported a 5% year-on-year growth in net profit for Q4 FY26 to Rs 5,113 crore, driven by a strong performance within its cigarettes business and FMCG-cigarettes segment.

articles.title: Nifty Bank rises 650 points as report says RBI unlikely to hike rates to defend rupee; Axis, ICICI, HDFC shares jump up to 2% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is considering various options to address inflation, which remains subdued despite the rupee's recent decline.  While the RBI has stated it will prioritize inflation over currency defense, economists at Standard Chartered predict rate hikes as early as June, citing rising crude prices. Interest rate swap markets are pricing in significant rate increases by the RBI, with some predicting a 50 basis point hike in June and more than 100 basis points over the next year.  The RBI's decision on whether to raise rates will be announced on June 5th, following its second meeting since the Iran-US conflict began.

articles.title: Amazon Uk Chief: ‘It’s not their fault’: Amazon UK boss says education system is failing young workers | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Amazon’s UK country manager, John Boumphrey, argued that the education system is failing to prepare young people for work, contributing to rising unemployment. He stated that businesses are struggling to recruit workers with the necessary skills despite a million young people being out of education, employment or training. Boumphrey called for work experience placements to become compulsory and closer cooperation between businesses, local authorities and further education colleges to address regional skills shortages.  He emphasized that Amazon is facing difficulty recruiting enough workers for technical and engineering roles due to automation and robotics expansion in its warehouses.

articles.title: LIC shares jump 5% after Q4 results, first-ever bonus issue. Here's what brokerages say - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: LIC, the state-run insurance company, reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 23,467 crore for the fourth quarter of FY26, marking a 23% year-on-year increase. The firm's net premium income rose 12% YoY to Rs 1.65 lakh crore. Citi and Bernstein have issued positive ratings on LIC shares, with Citi predicting an upside potential of over 84% and Bernstein a potential of more than 12%. JM Financial also maintains a "Buy" rating on LIC shares, raising its target price to Rs 960 apiece.  LIC's share price jumped 5% on Friday.

articles.title: Nykaa shares rally 4%, hit 52-week high after Q4. Here's what Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley are saying - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nykaa reported a 28% year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 2,648 crore for the March quarter, driven by strong growth in its beauty and fashion businesses. The company's gross merchandise value (GMV) also rose 28% year-on-year to Rs 5,241 crore. Nykaa CEO Falguni Nayar highlighted the company's multi-engine growth platform, with Beauty and Fashion businesses doubling their GMV in the past three years. Analysts from Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, and Elara Securities maintained positive ratings on the stock, citing strong revenue growth, profitability, and AI-driven efficiency improvements.

articles.title: Central Bank of India OFS: Govt to sell up to 8% stake in lender. Check key details - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The government, as part of the bank’s promoter group, will open an Offer for Sale (OFS) on May 22nd for non-retail investors and May 25th for retail investors. The OFS offers a floor price of Rs 31 per share, representing a discount of around 9.4% to the last closing price.  The government has set aside 10% of the total offer size for retail investors while mutual funds and insurance companies will receive 25%. The bank's net interest income rose 17.8% year-on-year, but its fourth-quarter net profit declined by 30%.

articles.title: Focus on infrastructure, agricultural productivity, developing clusters for export: U.P. State Transformation Commission CEO - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Uttar Pradesh is focusing on infrastructure development, agricultural productivity, and export-oriented clusters to bridge the income gap between Western and Eastern districts. Manoj Kumar Singh, CEO of the State Transformation Commission, highlighted the state's focus on infrastructure projects like the Ganga Expressway and Noida International Airport, aiming to develop Jewar as a cargo hub for agricultural exports. The UP-AGREES project, funded by the World Bank, aims to increase agricultural productivity in 28 low-income districts across the state.

articles.title: Guzman y Gomez exits US after succumbing to ‘graveyard’ for Australian fast food chains | Business | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Guzman y Gomez (GyG) is closing its US business after failing to establish a profitable presence. The Mexican-themed chain cited performance issues and the need for significant investment as reasons for the closure, which is expected to cost the company up to US$40 million. Steven Marks, founder and co-chief executive of GyG, acknowledged that despite efforts to differentiate its offerings, sales momentum did not improve. Analysts have previously described the US market as a "graveyard" for Australian fast food companies, citing challenges in competing with established chains like Chipotle.  GyG will continue to focus on Australia and expansion into Singapore and Japan.

articles.title: Rupee moves up after 10 days on likely RBI intervention - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Rupee strengthened against the dollar Thursday, closing at 96.20 per dollar after heavy sales by state-run banks likely on behalf of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to curb its depreciation.  Traders expect further intervention from the RBI and anticipate a moderation in the rupee's depreciation pressure as positive news emerges. DBS Bank expects the rupee to remain between 95-100 against the dollar for the rest of 2026, while India is considering various options, including raising interest rates, to stabilize its currency.

articles.title: Multi-asset funds reward tactical bets amid volatile market - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Multi-asset allocation funds saw a surge in popularity, with assets increasing to ₹1.87 lakh crore from ₹1.13 lakh crore last year.  This growth is attributed to investors seeking professional management as volatile equities and fluctuating gold and silver prices made traditional asset allocation less reliable. Kotak Multi Asset Allocation, Quant Multi Asset Allocation, DSP Multi Assset Allocation, HSBC Multi Asset Allocation and Bandhan Multi Asset Allocation were among the top performers in 2023, with their success hinging on accurate asset allocation strategies.  Investment experts emphasize that fund managers must remain adaptable and make selective bets within various market segments to navigate future market cycles effectively.

articles.title: Cigarette business weakness drags ITC margins in March quarter - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: ITC is implementing strategies to mitigate the impact of higher taxes on its cigarette business, aiming to protect market share and revenue growth. The company's stock has declined nearly 24% in 2026 due to concerns about illicit cigarette trade fueled by the tax increase. ITC acknowledges that past tax hikes have led to increased illicit activity, particularly in India, where it holds a significant portion of the legal market.  The recent tax hike may further widen price gaps and encourage illicit trade, impacting the company's profitability.

articles.title: Govt AGR relief, fresh funding fuel 61% rally in Vodafone Idea stock since April - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Aditya Birla group has injected ₹4,730 crore into Vodafone Idea (VIL), increasing its stake to 13% and boosting hopes of further bank financing. This follows a government revision of AGR liabilities to ₹64,046 crore, offering a more favorable repayment structure with a five-year moratorium. The infusion comes after a previous attempt in 2024 failed due to uncertainty surrounding AGR dues.  VIL's subscriber base has shrunk significantly but average revenue per user (ARPU) has increased, and data usage has grown.

articles.title: Labor MPs expect eventual concessions for startups after backlash to CGT changes | Tax | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Labor MPs are pushing for concessions on capital gains tax (CGT) for startups after a backlash to the budget fueled by memes. Some MPs believe the government will eventually agree to some form of concession, recognizing the unique challenges faced by these businesses and concerns about the new cost-base inflation model. Tim Ayres, the industry minister, has hinted at potential concessions but has not confirmed any timeline or specific plans.  Anthony Albanese and Jim Chalmers, the Prime Minister and Treasurer respectively, have been criticized for failing to adequately explain the complex tax changes, with some MPs expressing concerns about misinformation online.

articles.title: Foreign investors continue to pull out from financials in first half of May - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Banks are facing headwinds from higher bond yields and increased provisioning requirements, leading to volatile return ratios. Overseas investors have sold over ₹91,000 crore worth of Indian financial stocks in the first four months of 2023, citing better opportunities in other emerging markets.  While foreign inflows into the services sector are expected due to the MSCI rebalancing next week, analysts suggest that these trends will likely persist.

articles.title: West Asia crisis hurting Indian tea exporters - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Indian Tea Association (ITA) officials reported that the West Asia conflict has significantly impacted tea exports, with 87% of India's total exports concentrated in countries around the Gulf of Persia and the Gulf of Oman. The conflict, which began in February, has led to declining export volumes between January and March compared to 2025, as well as increased freight rates and shipping costs. Dinesh Bihani, secretary of the Guwahati Tea Auction Buyers’ Association, stated that the economic uncertainty in West Asia is causing importers to be cautious about buying tea, leading to softer demand and price pressure on both domestic and international markets.  The industry remains hopeful for a recovery in trade flows and consumption once stability returns.

articles.title: UK launches ‘Great British Summer Savings’ to ease family costs | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The UK government launched the “Great British Summer Savings” scheme to help families afford summer activities.  From June 25th to September 1st, 2026, VAT will be temporarily reduced from 20 percent to 5 percent on children’s meals, family tickets for entertainment venues, and admission tickets to attractions like theme parks and museums. The program is estimated to cost £300 million ($403 million). Prime Minister Keir Starmer and Chancellor Rachel Reeves stated the initiative aims to ease pressure on household budgets while supporting struggling businesses.

articles.title: Govt reopens offshore oil frontier - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik witnessed the signing of production sharing agreements (PSAs) and exploration licences (ELs) for 23 offshore blocks awarded in the Offshore Bid Round 2025. The awarding of these blocks, located in the Indus and Makran basins, attracted an initial investment of $82 million and is expected to reach $1 billion if exploration activities progress to the second phase. Mari Energies, a leading participant, emerged as the most active participant with 18 blocks awarded as operator or joint venture partner. The government aims to revitalize offshore exploration, attract foreign and domestic investment, and reduce reliance on imported energy through this initiative.

articles.title: MQM-P leader Khalid Maqbool made member of Economic Coordination Committee - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has approved the addition of Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui, leader of the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P), as a member of the Economic Coordination Committee (ECC).  The PMO statement noted that this decision follows a meeting between Siddiqui and Shehbaz Sharif where budget proposals were discussed and the overall political situation was reviewed. The ECC is responsible for handling urgent economic decisions and coordinating financial and economic policies across government departments.

articles.title: MPs urged to ignore fearmongering and pass Labor’s ‘long overdue’ negative gearing and CGT changes | Housing | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Labor's proposed changes to negative gearing and capital gains tax are being urged by Australian peak community and housing groups as a way to improve fairness for renters and young homebuyers. The reforms, which include limiting new negative gearing to new-builds and grandfathering existing properties, aim to rebalance the housing market towards first-time buyers.  The changes have been welcomed by social and housing groups who predict they will improve housing stability for renters and encourage long-term investment in housing. However, some economists are concerned about potential impacts on home values and rents, while property lobbyists have raised concerns about misinformation surrounding the reforms.

articles.title: Nykaa Q4 Results: Cons profit surges 286% YoY to Rs 78 crore, revenue rises 28% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nykaa's parent company reported a 28% increase in revenue to Rs 2,648 crore for the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026 (Q4FY26), driven by a 26% rise in net revenue to Rs 10,022 crore. The company's gross merchandising value (GMV) grew 28% year-on-year to Rs 5,241 crore, marking the 14th consecutive quarter of growth. Nykaa also saw a significant increase in its EBITDA and PAT, with EBITDA rising 67% YoY to Rs 223 crore and PAT surging 183% to Rs 204 crore for the fiscal year.

articles.title: Nvidia's latest record earnings fail to impress investors
articles.rephrased_article: Nvidia, the world's most valuable company, reported record quarterly earnings with revenue exceeding expectations and a significant increase in net income. Despite strong performance driven by data center growth, shares fell after-hours as investors anticipate slowing growth and increased competition. Nvidia is forecasting continued revenue growth to reach $91 billion in the second quarter, while returning cash to shareholders through dividends and share buybacks.  However, analysts suggest that investor expectations for continued hypergrowth may have led to an early sell-off.

articles.title: Paytm block deal: SAIF Partners, others likely to sell stake worth Rs 963 crore, says report - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: SAIF Partners, a global investment bank, is reportedly arranging a block deal sale of shares in One 97 Communications, the parent company of Paytm. The transaction is expected to raise $100 million from existing shareholders.  The move follows a significant stock price recovery for Paytm, driven by improved operational metrics and investor confidence in the digital payments sector.

articles.title: Walmart warns US shoppers are cutting spending as higher petrol prices bite
articles.rephrased_article: Walmart has warned that higher petrol prices are causing US consumers to cut spending, leading to a slowdown in sales growth between May and July. The retail giant expects this trend to continue as the effect of tax cuts from President Trump's One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) fades away. John David Rainey, Walmart's finance boss, stated that while higher tax returns initially offset pressure from rising fuel costs, they are now diminishing, putting consumers under more strain.  Walmart is closely monitoring petrol prices and expects them to remain high in the coming months, potentially impacting food prices due to supply chain disruptions.

articles.title: LIC announces 1:1 bonus issue, sets May 29 as record date - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: LIC, the State-owned insurance company, announced a 1:1 share swap for existing shareholders. The company reported strong Q4 earnings with a 23% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 23,467 crore. LIC's board recommended a final dividend of Rs 10 per share for the financial year 2025-26.  The company also saw significant growth in its net premium income, VNB, and assets under management (AUM).

articles.title: Honasa Consumer Q4 results: Profit more than doubles to Rs 69 cr; co declares Rs 3 dividend - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Honasa Consumer, the parent company of Mamaearth, reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue of Rs 682 crore in Q4 FY26, driven by strong growth across key categories and a robust offline distribution network. The company's EBITDA reached Rs 77 crore, marking its highest-ever quarterly operating profit.  Honasa Consumer also announced a maiden final dividend of Rs 3 per equity share, representing 51.2% of FY26 standalone profit after tax. Chairman and CEO Varun Alagh attributed the company's success to investments in AI-led content systems, research and development, product innovation, and distribution infrastructure.

articles.title: Sebi proposes changes to pre-open listing session of IPOs for better price discovery - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sebi, the Securities and Exchange Board of India, has released a consultation paper seeking public feedback on proposed changes to the Call Auction Session framework used for relisted stocks. The regulator cited concerns that the current system, which uses dummy price bands and base price calculations, is leading to artificial price suppression and persistent buying pressure once trading begins. Sebi wants to understand if these mechanisms need modification to improve efficiency and reduce distortions in price discovery.  The consultation paper outlines how equilibrium prices are determined during the pre-open session for IPOs and relisted stocks.

articles.title: Boo of Jobs: Real anger about Artificial Intelligence at US convocations - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Across the United States, commencement speakers who mention artificial intelligence are facing backlash from graduates and communities concerned about job displacement and the uneven distribution of benefits from the AI boom.  At several universities, graduates booed speakers who discussed the future of AI, expressing frustration over potential job losses and concerns about the impact of data centers on their communities. While proponents of AI highlight its potential for economic growth and innovation, critics argue that the gains are not evenly distributed and raise questions about democratic consent in the face of rapid technological change.  This growing public skepticism towards AI reflects a broader societal concern over the impact of technology on employment and social equity.

articles.title: Over 15 MF schemes cut exposure to these 10 stocks in April ’26. Do you own any? - Stock Ideas | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Mutual funds significantly reduced their holdings in 14 stocks during April 2026, a trend driven by geopolitical uncertainties and market volatility.  The analysis revealed that nearly 15 stocks saw a decrease in mutual fund exposure compared to March 2026. Notably, seven of these stocks have experienced negative returns so far in CY26, with some declines exceeding 60%.

articles.title: Select SFBs and MFI players positioned for earnings upside: Rajiv Mehta - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Rajiv Mehta, from Yes Securities, stated that while the NBFC sector faces external risks, underlying credit performance has remained stable. He highlighted microfinance and select housing finance players as attractive sub-segments within the broader financial space.  He noted strong collections in lending categories, but cautioned that macro risks remain a key monitorable. Mehta believes the strongest cyclical recovery is unfolding in microfinance and microfinance-linked small finance banks, citing renewed growth momentum in affordable housing companies. He also recommended focusing on select lenders with large microfinance portfolios, such as Ujjivan, CreditAccess Grameen, and Fusion.  While acknowledging a positive credit cycle, Mehta cautioned that macro uncertainties could delay the pace of improvement due to inflation and affordability stress.

articles.title: GE Vernova T&D emerges as top BSE Power multibagger with 164% returns; should investors buy now? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: GE Vernova T&D India shares have surged following strong Q4FY26 earnings, reporting an 89% year-on-year jump in net profit and a 42% revenue increase. The company's robust operational momentum is attributed to factors like improved margins and healthy order inflows. Analysts at HDFC Securities and PL Capital have revised their EPS estimates upwards, maintaining a "Buy" rating on the stock with target prices of Rs 5,200 and Rs 4,650 respectively.  Despite this positive outlook, some analysts are concerned about the recent share price rally and have downgraded the stock to "Accumulate".

articles.title: Ola Electric shares can crash up to 35%, warns Emkay after seeing Q4 results - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Ola Electric, led by Bhavish Aggarwal, reported a consolidated net loss of Rs 500 crore for the January-March quarter of the financial year 2026, down 42.5% from the previous year.  While the company saw some sequential volume improvement and market share gains, Emkay analysts believe Ola's recovery will be a long process due to competition from incumbents like Ather Energy and TVS Motor Company. The brokerage firm maintains its 'Sell' call for Ola Electric Mobility shares but raised its target price to Rs 25 from Rs 20.

articles.title: Apollo Micro Systems shares rally 22% in 3 days after strong Q4 results. Should you buy? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Apollo Micro Systems shares surged nearly 6% to a new 52-week high on Thursday, driven by strong quarterly and annual financial performance. The defense player reported a 163% year-on-year increase in net profit for the fourth quarter of FY26, alongside a significant rise in revenue.  The company attributed its success to acquisitions, licensing agreements, and record order bookings. Analysts predict continued upward momentum for the stock, recommending fresh buying with a stop loss at Rs 340.

articles.title: Jubilant Foodworks shares crash 8% after Domino's India operator's Q4 results. What spooked investors? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Jubilant FoodWorks, the operator of Domino's Pizza, reported a 66% year-on-year increase in net profit for the January-March quarter of the financial year 2026. Revenue from operations grew 19% YoY to Rs 2,499 crore during the quarter. The company recommended a dividend of Rs 1.2 per share (60%) with a face value of Rs 2 each for the financial year that ended on March 31, 2026, subject to shareholder approval at the upcoming AGM. Despite temporary LPG supply constraints impacting operations, Jubilant FoodWorks managed the situation effectively and expects normalized supply in Q1FY27.  Analysts from various brokerage firms have varying opinions on the company's performance, with some maintaining a "Buy" rating while others express concerns about near-term margin pressures.

articles.title: Mega merger incoming: Should you buy PFC, REC shares ahead of merger? Here's what analysts say - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nirmala Sitharaman, the Union Finance Minister, announced plans to restructure Power Finance Corporation (PFC) and Rural Electrification Corporation (REC) for streamlined operations. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved a proposal where PFC acquired 52.63% of the government's holding in REC, consolidating them into a single balance sheet.  Analysts suggest investors consider staggered exposure to PFC and REC as the merger process is subject to regulatory approvals and structural adjustments. While PFC offers better visibility due to its parent status, REC presents a merger-arbitrage opportunity with higher event risk depending on the swap ratio.

articles.title: Ketan Parekh Case: Sebi sends show cause notice to 6 Capital Group FPIs - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sebi has initiated legal proceedings against Capital Group, alleging that its traders, James Vincent Cheng and Terence Tsai, leaked sensitive information about impending trades to Salgaocar, who then shared it with Ketan Parekh for front-running the market. The regulator claims that this resulted in illicit gains for those involved.  The investigation covers a period from January 1, 2021, to June 20, 2023, and Sebi alleges that Capital Group failed to maintain confidentiality regarding its trading intentions.

articles.title: Reeves to promise free summer bus rides for children and food tariff cuts in living costs package | Economics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Rachel Reeves, the chancellor, will announce a package of measures to address rising inflation caused by the Iran conflict. These include free bus rides for children aged 15 and under during August as part of the "Great British summer savings scheme" and the removal of tariffs on certain food imports. The Treasury estimates the cost of these measures at £400 million, with details about funding to be outlined on Thursday. Keir Starmer has also announced postponements to fuel duty increases and a vehicle tax holiday for lorry drivers.

articles.title: RBI proposes rules to let lenders disable phones for loan defaults - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has proposed amendments to its Responsible Business Conduct Directions that would allow banks to restrict functionalities of borrowers' mobile devices only under tightly regulated conditions. The draft guidelines, effective from October 1, 2026, specify that restrictions can be imposed only after a loan becomes 90 days past due and following multiple notices to the borrower.  The RBI has also introduced stricter rules for loan recovery, including mandatory certification for recovery agents, public disclosure of empanelled agencies, and prohibitions on assigning cases while grievances remain unresolved. The draft norms also prohibit banks from accessing or storing data on borrowers' phones and impose restrictions on recovery staff conduct.

articles.title: Sensex gains 560 points, Nifty above 23,800. Key factors behind today's Dalal Street rally - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Sensex and Nifty 50 gained significantly on Thursday, driven by a combination of factors including cooled bond yields, declining oil prices, and hopes for an Iran-US peace deal.  The Rupee strengthened against the US dollar, while global markets rallied as some vessels resumed passage through the Strait of Hormuz. However, foreign investors remained net sellers in Indian equities, raising concerns about sustained market strength.

articles.title: Australia’s unemployment rate jumps to 4.5% in ‘tentative signs labour market is buckling’ | Unemployment | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Australia’s unemployment rate surged to 4.5% in April, marking the highest level in nearly four-and-a-half years, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics. The unexpected decline in employed individuals contributed to this increase, prompting economists to question whether the Reserve Bank of Australia will raise interest rates again.  The jobless rate remains below pre-pandemic levels but has been on an upward trajectory since late 2022, and financial markets are now factoring in a smaller chance of future interest rate hikes.

articles.title: Lenskart shares rise 2% after Q4 profit slips; revenue jumps 46% YoY - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Lenskart, despite a profit decline, reported strong operational growth in FY26. Revenue increased 32% to Rs 9,002 crore, driven by a 46% year-on-year rise in revenue from operations to Rs 2,516 crore.  The company conducted 23.8 million eye tests globally, with India experiencing strong same-store sales growth (SSSG) and expanding its footprint to 157 new cities. International operations also performed well, with international revenue growing 30% and EBITDA margin improving to 7%.

articles.title: IMF wraps up Pakistan visit following talks with authorities on reforms, budget - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission concluded talks with Pakistan authorities, focusing on economic developments, fiscal plans for the next financial year, and progress on reforms under its IMF-supported programs. The mission, led by Iva Petrova, discussed disruptions from the Middle East conflict, budget formulation, and ongoing reform efforts in areas like energy, state-owned enterprises, and financial sector reforms.  The authorities reaffirmed their commitment to a primary surplus target of two percent of GDP and emphasized efforts to broaden the tax base and improve fiscal management. The IMF mission also highlighted the importance of maintaining an appropriately tight monetary policy stance and building a deeper foreign exchange market.  Discussions on structural reforms and progress under the Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF) were also covered, with the next mission expected in the second half of 2026.

articles.title: Samsung strike on hold as workers push for AI bonus
articles.rephrased_article: Samsung Electronics reached a tentative pay agreement with its largest union, averting a planned strike that could have disrupted the global technology industry. The deal will be voted on by union members from May 22nd to 27th and includes bonuses for memory chip workers at least six times higher than those received by employees in other units. Samsung had proposed bonuses of 607% of annual salary for memory chip workers, while other employees would receive only 50% to 100%. The company's stock price rose after the agreement was reached, and the South Korean court granted an injunction to prevent a strike from disrupting operations.

articles.title: Fed Minutes: More officials warned of rate hike scenario - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Many officials at the Federal Open Market Committee meeting last month expressed concerns about persistent inflation, prompting a debate over whether to signal an interest-rate increase.  The minutes of the April 28-29 meeting show that while some participants believed rate cuts would eventually be warranted, most favored firming up policy if inflation remained above 2%. The decision to retain the easing bias in the post-meeting statement was a closer call than at the previous meeting and could potentially be revisited.  Incoming Fed Chair Kevin Warsh will face this challenge as he takes over from outgoing Chair Jerome Powell.

articles.title: Parle Industries hits upper circuit amid ‘Melody’ confusion - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Parle Industries shares surged 5% on Wednesday after a social media video showed Prime Minister Narendra Modi giving a 'Melody' toffee to his Italian counterpart, Giorgia Meloni. The stock's trading volume spiked significantly, exceeding its two-week average. This is not an isolated incident; similar mix-ups have occurred in the past with companies like LG Electronics India and Tata Motors, highlighting the potential for confusion among retail investors during market volatility.

articles.title: Manchester shows biggest fall in inner-city deprivation in boost for Burnham | Economics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Manchester has experienced the largest decline in inner-city deprivation among UK towns and cities, according to a report by the Centre for Cities.  Between 2010 and 2025, Manchester saw a 17 percentage point fall in deprivation rates, exceeding other major cities like London and Liverpool. This success is attributed to the city's devolved powers and interventionist economic policies championed by Andy Burnham, who is vying for leadership of the Labour Party.

articles.title: Long-term SIPs deliver consistent gains as market volatility eases over time - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: A study by Whiteoak Capital found that SIP returns diverged in shorter holding periods, narrowing over longer durations.  For a three-year horizon, returns ranged from 55.6% gains to 24.6% losses, but for investments of eight years or more, all SIPs made gains and did not experience losses. Madhu Nair, CEO of Union Mutual Fund, recommends a minimum investment period of 10 years to benefit from rupee cost averaging and navigate market cycles.

articles.title: Why CEA Anantha Nageswaran says India is facing a ‘Live Balance of Payments Stress Test’ - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: India is facing a significant strain on its balance of payments (BoP) due to rising global crude oil prices and geopolitical tensions. The country's heavy reliance on imported energy has led to a surge in import costs, widening the current account deficit and weakening the rupee. Economists warn that this situation mirrors past crises like the 1991 balance of payments crisis and could require long-term adjustments.  HSBC suggests India needs to attract sustainable capital inflows while reducing its current account deficit. India's economic stability hinges on managing these challenges effectively, particularly in the face of global shifts impacting trade, capital flows, and energy security.

articles.title: Bound for Mars, Elon Musk's SpaceX unveils filing for blockbuster IPO - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX, the world's largest space business, is poised to become the first trillion-dollar U.S. market debut and could set a precedent for other monumental IPOs in the coming months. The company's planned listing on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol 'SPCX' could value it at $1.75 trillion, making its founder, Elon Musk, the first trillionaire in history.  The sale would cement SpaceX as one of the world's most valuable publicly traded companies and solidify its position as a leader in space exploration with plans for lunar and Mars missions and expansion of its Starlink satellite internet business.

articles.title: India needs to raise R&D spending to 2 pc of GDP by 2035 to boost manufacturing: Report - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Careedge Ratings released a report highlighting India's manufacturing sector challenges.  The report states that India's R&D spending is only 0.6-0.7% of GDP, significantly lower than global peers like the US (3%), China (2.5%), and South Korea (up to 5%). This low investment hinders growth in value-added production, contributing to a decline in manufacturing's share of GDP from 16% in 2015 to 13% in 2024.  The report recommends increasing R&D spending to 2% by 2035, along with greater private sector participation, stronger innovation ecosystems, and improved research-to-commercialization pipelines.  It also emphasizes the need for strengthening STEM education, deeper industry-academia collaboration, higher private-sector R&D investment, and integrated innovation-led industrial ecosystems to enhance India's global competitiveness.

articles.title: PSX gains 1,900 points, maintaining renewed buying - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) experienced a significant gain of over 1,900 points on Wednesday, closing at 164,831.42 points, driven by investor confidence boosted by easing tensions between Iran and the United States, along with lower international oil prices.  Heavyweight stocks like Meezan Bank Limited (MEBL), Fauji Fertiliser Company Limited (FFC), and Pakistan Petroleum Limited (PPL) contributed significantly to the market's bullish momentum. The positive performance was also supported by increased trading volume of 386 million shares, with SSGC leading the way.

articles.title: AI boom: Global stock market order shuffles as Taiwan, South Korea overtake Western giants - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The South Korean Kospi stock market has experienced a significant surge, more than tripling in less than 18 months, surpassing even the Nasdaq's bull run in the 1990s. This rally has propelled South Korea to eighth place globally in equity-market capitalisation rankings, overtaking the UK.  While analysts point to the sustainability of this rally compared to the dotcom bubble, concerns remain about the concentration of capital into a few AI firms, particularly TSMC and Samsung Electronics. The surge in Asian markets is also attracting foreign investment, with some analysts suggesting it may be driven by interest in AI and semiconductor themes.
